Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verses 1–2:

(p-224) Surat Hud (peace be upon him)

Its central theme is the description of the Book as perfected (ihkam) and detailed (tafsil) in both its modes of glad tidings (bishara) and warning (nidhara). This requires of its Sender, glory be to Him, that He place everything in its most fitting position and execute it whatever He wills, which necessitates power over everything. The most suitable element in it for this purpose is what is mentioned in the context of the story of Hud (peace be upon him) of the rulings on glad tidings and warning, regarding the immediate and the deferred, and the explicit, decisive statement concerning treatment through prompt action, looking toward the greatest axis of the surah: ﴿So perhaps you would leave out some of what is revealed to you﴾ [Hud: 12], and the care for every creature and the power over everything, including resurrection and other things, which necessitates knowledge of every object of knowledge, the necessary consequence of which is exclusive sovereignty. [The reason why each of the two surahs is specifically named by its name will come in al-Ahqaf.]

"In the name of Allah" – i.e., the One who possesses complete knowledge, perfect wisdom and all power; "the Most Gracious" – to all His creation, by the generality of glad tidings and warning; "the Most Merciful" – to the people of His friendship, by protection in following His path. ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra.﴾

When the preceding surah ended – as you see – with the exhortation to follow the Book, to adhere to it, and to be patient with what follows from its bitter hardships which lead to the wastelands of good, relying on the One characterized by majesty, greatness and perfection, this surah began by describing Him with what makes one desire Him. After the indication to renewing the challenge by defiance, as was previously established (p-225) in al-Baqarah, He said: ﴿A Book﴾, i.e., a great book comprising every good. Then He described it by saying: ﴿its verses have been made firm﴾, the verb being in the passive form to explain that its making firm is a matter already completed [in the easiest manner from Him, glory be to Him], and it has been perfected to a degree beyond which there is no increase. ﴿Its verses﴾, i.e., they have been perfected with a perfection in which there is no deficiency. So He who sent them down does not diminish them by abrogating them all by another book, nor does anyone else have the ability to diminish any part of them or to criticize any part of their eloquence or fluency with anything that would be accepted. The meaning of ﴿muhkamat﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7] in Al 'Imran is the absence of resemblance (tashabuh).

Since detail (tafsil) has a rank that is at the utmost of greatness, the particle of delay was brought, so He said: ﴿Then﴾, i.e., after this lofty rank, in which no other book shares in the whole of it, there was given to it a rank far higher than it, such that no book shares with it in any part of it. That is: ﴿it has been detailed﴾, i.e., there were made for it – while being detailed into lawful and unlawful, narratives and parables – junctures and endings by which it is distinguished from what comes after it and [what] comes before it, from which are understood numerous sciences, important knowledge, indications to lofty states, pure sweet springs, and stations of every healing cure, just as necklaces are detailed with pearls. This detail is not shared in any part of it by any of the earlier books; rather, they are integrated without any junctures, as those who study them know, and what I have quoted from them throughout this book suffices for knowing this. (p-226) How fitting is the conclusion of this verse for firmness and detail, with His words: ﴿from One who is Wise and Acquainted﴾: its verses were sent down firm and detailed, while originating from a presence that is the most wondrous of presences proceeding from a God, ﴿Wise, All-Aware﴾, terminating with you, while you are the highest of people in every attribute, therefore its firmness and its detail cannot be matched. We sent you with it, saying: ﴿that you worship none but Allah﴾, i.e., in any way whatsoever, ﴿none but Allah﴾, i.e., the Greatest God.

Since this is the greatest part of what he (ﷺ) was sent with and its core, He resumed the report that He sent him, glory be to Him, emphasizing it [on account of their denial], so He said: ﴿Indeed I am﴾. Since his (ﷺ) sending was for the mercy of the worlds, He placed their pronoun first, saying: ﴿to you from Him﴾, i.e., specifically, then He summed up the whole Qur'an in his two attributes, may Allah bless him, by saying [placing first what is most fitting to the conclusion of the preceding surah with patience]: ﴿a warner and a bringer of glad tidings﴾ [complete in each of the two attributes to the utmost perfection]. This arrangement is indicated by His saying at the beginning of the preceding surah: ﴿Is it a wonder to the people that We revealed to a man from among them: warn the people﴾ [Yunus: 2]. With its explanation, when He connected to it His saying: ﴿And We sent Noah to his people, [saying] Indeed I am﴾ [Hud: 25], We joined it to it; and its explicit mention is for the benefit of its connection, as will come, God willing. What indicates that "la" (do not) is a prohibitive particle governing "ta'budu" (worship) is that "an istaghfiru" (that you seek forgiveness) is coordinated with it. It has become clear from (p-227) the allusion and explicit statement of this, and the explicit statement of what is in the rest of the surah, that its purpose is to describe the Book with firmness and detail in a way that defeats creation, because it is from One whose knowledge encompasses all and whose power is complete; He is perfect in wisdom, restoring creation for recompense just as He originated them for action. Therefore it is obligatory to single Him out in worship, to comply with all His commands, and not to leave any of them out in hope of someone's approval or fear of someone's turning away, nor to fear anyone else, nor to rely on anything other than Him. Upon this all the prophets proceeded, and all the messengers, may Allah bless them all.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verse 3:

Since it had been stated earlier that he is a warner and a bearer of good news, He followed this with what encompasses both matters, by His saying, coordinated with ﴿that you worship none but Allah﴾ [Hud: 2], indicating that no one can measure Allah with the measure He deserves: ﴿And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾. That is, seek, with sincerity in worship, that the One who has bestowed favour upon you forgive you what you have neglected. By the particle of delay (thumma, "then") He indicated the high rank of repentance (tawba), and that there is no way to seek forgiveness except through it, so He said: ﴿then turn back to Him in repentance﴾. That is, return with the outward and the inward, a return with no coming back to what was left. [And if by it is meant continuance, then its sublime rank is not hidden.] ﴿He will grant you enjoyment﴾ [that is, He will extend your enjoyment of life, extending it, from matana al-nahar (the day rose high), and al-duha (the forenoon) reached its extreme; and amtaʿahu Allah bi-kadha (Allah granted him such-and-such) means He let him remain and raised him until he reaches his youth]; and [since] enjoyment (al-tamtiʿ), which is complete provision in which there is no turbidity, is only in Paradise, therefore the verbal noun was made ﴿provision﴾, and it was placed in the position of "granting enjoyment" (tamtiʿan), this verbal noun, and He described it by His saying: ﴿good﴾, to indicate that it is the utmost that befits this abode. And the bounty the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) received in the time of ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), of success in conquest, abundance of worldly goods and ease of living, was indeed like this. ﴿Until﴾, that is, extending until ﴿a specified term﴾, that is, in His knowledge, either by death for each one, or by the expiry of the term He set for the blessing He has indicated. ﴿And He will give every person of merit his merit﴾, that is, every person doing virtuous deeds, ﴿his merit﴾, that is, the reward for what he intended by his deed in the manner of bestowal from Him, glorified is He; for it is not obligatory upon Allah for anyone to be owed anything, and yet it is according to bestowal: a good deed is rewarded tenfold. Ibn Masʿud said: "Whoever his units outweigh his tens has perished."

When the good news had concluded, affirmed, He followed it with a warning, frightening them from it, out of kindness to the servants and to win their sympathy, and so He said: ﴿But if you turn away﴾, that is, you burden yourselves against what Allah has created them upon of the soundness of the fitra (natural disposition) and ease of submission, by turning away, even to its lowest degree, as indicated by the omission of the ta' (the verb being read as "if they turn away" rather than "if you turn away"). ﴿then I fear for you﴾, that is, and the intelligent person keeps far from what is feared, ﴿the punishment of a great Day﴾, that is, because of the greatness of the punishment in it, from One who is able to destroy you. He singled out the name "Lord" to remind them of the blessings He has bestowed in bringing into existence, creating and nurturing. And since seeking forgiveness, which is asking for pardon, is desired in itself, but is not accepted unless it is joined with repentance, He linked it with "then" (thumma), indicating the great rank of repentance and its station, and if by it is meant persistence in it, then its sublime rank is not hidden. In the expression of action by "merit" there is an indication that the obligation has only been placed upon what is within one's capacity, together with its being among the highest of noble qualities, because merit (fadl) in origin is what exceeds a person and what he exerts of noble dispositions. What is like this is at the summit of firmness, because it prevents the act from corruption. And the wise (hakim) is from wisdom (hikma), which is knowledge of what unites the act of what prevents it from corruption and deficiency, and by it the good is distinguished from the ugly, and the sound from the corrupt. The verse has indicated that seeking forgiveness and repentance are the cause of abundance: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 66], and that turning away is the cause of constriction, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed a servant is deprived of provision because of a sin he commits."

﴿And He will give every person of merit his merit﴾ indicates the reward of the Hereafter, so repentance is the cause of a good life in this world and the Hereafter.

Imam Abu Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr said in his book on the correspondence (munasaba) of this surah with the one before it: Since Surat Yunus had included, among the verses of alerting and stirring the natural dispositions, of admonitions, of frightening, threatening, instilling dread and inducing desire, of rebuking the polytheists and the deniers, of cutting them off, of informing of proceeding according to the precedents, and of the obligation of entrusting and submission, what no other surah has included in its like, because these aims recur in it, and the cause of this recurrence in it, Allah knows best, is that it was followed by the seven long surahs (al-sab' al-tiwal). It has already been noted that Surat al-Anʿam has the character of completing the explanation of the state of those who deviate from the straight path in their various conditions. Then Surat al-Anʿam completed what had been referred to of the states of the earlier nations, as has been mentioned, and expanded upon what had been summarized of their affair. Then it followed that with addressing those who responded to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and warned and admonished, and it uncovered the state of those among their enemies who had become entangled with them, the hypocrites. The aim of this was completed in the two surahs al-Anfal and Bara'a. Then the address returned to the method of calling to Allah and warning of His punishment after expanding upon what preceded, so it was a context for emphasizing fear and dread, since that comes after the expansion of a state and the clarifying of proofs. Therefore Surat Yunus included from this what no other included. Do you not see its opening with His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah﴾ [Yunus: 3], etc.? The correspondence of this opening is the calling of creation to Allah in Surat al-Baqara with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord﴾ [al-Baqara: 21]. Then they are alerted here as they were alerted there, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "Then bring a surah like it"﴾ [Yunus: 38]. Then the admonitions, the rebukes, and the indications of the states of the deniers and the obstinate became emphatic. Of the alerting are: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah﴾ [Yunus: 3]; ﴿It is He who made the sun﴾ [Yunus: 5]; ﴿Indeed, in the alternation of night and day﴾ [Yunus: 6]; ﴿Say, "Is there any of your partners who begins creation and then repeats it?"﴾ [Yunus: 34]; ﴿Say, "Is there any of your partners who guides to the truth?"﴾ [Yunus: 35]; ﴿Say, "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth"﴾ [Yunus: 101], and others besides these. And in this manner the admonitions and aims referred to in this surah recurred, up to His saying: ﴿O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord﴾ [Yunus: 108]. Thus there resulted from Surat al-Aʿraf, al-Anfal, Bara'a and Yunus the detailing of what had been summarized in what preceded them, just as there resulted from what preceded the detailing of the states of the travellers and those who deviate. When all this was established, He followed the whole with His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been perfected and then detailed from the presence of the Wise, the Acquainted﴾ [Hud: 1]. And consider the correspondence of bringing these two noble names, which are "the Wise, the Acquainted," then consider the harmony of the beginning of the surah with His saying: ﴿O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord﴾ [Yunus: 108]. His saying had already preceded: ﴿There has come to you an admonition from your Lord﴾ [Yunus: 57]. So He followed His saying: ﴿The truth has come to you from your Lord﴾ [Yunus: 108] with His saying at the beginning of Surat Hud: ﴿A Book whose verses have been perfected and then detailed﴾ [Hud: 1]. So it is as if it is in the context of clarifying the truth and admonition. And when it is perfected and detailed, it is right that it be a healing for what is in the breasts, and guidance and mercy for the believers, and right that they be rebuked by His saying: ﴿Rather, they denied what they did not encompass in knowledge﴾ [Yunus: 39]. It is astonishing how they remain in confusion despite its perfection and detailing, but ﴿those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe﴾ [Yunus: 96]. Consider His saying, glorified is He, at the end of this surah: ﴿And all of the news of the messengers We relate to you is that by which We strengthen your heart. And there has come to you in these the truth and an admonition and a reminder for the believers﴾ [Hud: 120]. So the whole Book is truth, admonition and reminder. The indication, Allah knows best what He intended, is to what has been established of the allusion to the completeness of the explanation of the straight path, the obligations of its followers in taking and abandoning, and the mention of the states of those who deviate in their various ways, the differences of their desires and aims. The worst of them is Iblis, for he is their follower and the one who says to all of them, in Allah's report: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke it to you﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]. His affair and story have been expounded in al-Baqara and al-Aʿraf in a manner that facilitates for the believers caution against him, and makes them aware of him. Mention was made of the Jews, the Christians, the polytheists, the Sabians, the hypocrites and others, and the sin committed by each group was detailed, just as the people of the straight path were comprehensively mentioned, from among the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous, and their states were detailed in beginning, end, obligation and abandonment, which clarified their path and identified their party and group: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾ [al-Anʿam: 90]. And the states of the nations with their prophets were mentioned, and each nation was seized for its sin in detail. The beginning of creation was mentioned in the story of Adam (peace be upon him), and the state of the angels in submission and compliance; and the group of jinn was mentioned, believing and disbelieving; and the matter of the Hereafter, the end of the states of creatures and their settling in the Hereafter; and the repetition of calling creation to Allah, exalted is He, in hope for Him and mercy; and informing creation of what He, glorified is He, is, and of the sublime attributes and the most beautiful names that are due to Him; and He alerted the servants to take heed, and they learned the methods of reasoning, were made to desire and to fear, were given good news and warning, and were informed of the need of all creatures, in their entirety, for Him, glorified is He, as He is the sole one who created them, along with what lies between that which the creatures cannot count or encompass: ﴿And Allah says the truth, and He guides to the way﴾ [al-Ahzab: 4]. When all this had preceded in the seven long surahs and what follows them, He followed that with His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been perfected and then detailed from the presence of the Wise, the Acquainted﴾ [Hud: 1]. Then He followed this with an allusion to three divisions upon which the verses of the Books revolve: the division of divinity (al-ilahiyya), the division of messengerhood (al-risala), and the division of obligations (al-takalif). As for the first, it was indicated by His saying: ﴿that you worship none but Allah﴾ [Hud: 2]. As for the division of messengerhood, it was indicated by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good news﴾ [Hud: 2]. As for the division of obligations, it was indicated by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn back to Him in repentance﴾. These three divisions are those upon which the verses of the Qur'an revolve, and upon them the noble surah is based. When the complete treatment of all of this had been achieved in what preceded, and there remained no ground for doubt for the obstinate, nor any attachment for the denier, and the truth became clear and manifest, the Glorified and Exalted said: ﴿And there has come to you in these the truth﴾ [Hud: 120], indicating the completeness of the aim, the clarification of what is sought, and the full exposition of the knowledge through the clarity of the way. It has become clear from this how the noble surah corresponds to what precedes it. Among what bears witness to this, Allah knows best, is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord, and whom a witness from Him recites?﴾ [Hud: 17], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So remain upright as you have been commanded, and [so too] those who have turned back with you, and do not transgress﴾ [Hud: 112]. [Your way has become clear, and your party and group have attained success.] ﴿And do not incline toward those who have wronged, lest the Fire touch you﴾ [Hud: 113]. You have known their path and their end, so the way of the truth has become manifest. How could one who has firmly committed himself to its course among the creatures go astray! Its parallel is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And there has come to you in these the truth﴾ [Hud: 120], following what He, glorified is He, mentioned: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ [Ghafir: 16], and His saying: ﴿The Day when no soul will possess anything for another soul, and the command that Day belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Infitar: 19]. So consider [that], and Allah is the One sought for help. End.

When those who were warned were frightened by the Great Day, it was as though they had said: "What is this Day?" So the answer was: "The Day when they will return to Him." And since they might understand "return" to mean merely death and becoming dust, He alerted them that it is not in the sense they imagine, but in the sense of their being restored as they were. So He said: ﴿To Allah﴾, that is, to the King who alone encompasses everything in power and knowledge, ﴿is your return﴾, that is: [your return, its time and its place, for the sake of reckoning], not to dust or anything else. [He is All-Knowing of everything, and from Him is your beginning, so take provision for the Hereafter.] He made the verse-ending (fasila) a judge over the intended meaning, saying: ﴿And He﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿is over everything﴾, that is, every possible thing, ﴿Powerful﴾, that is, reaching full power, because they acknowledge His power over things greater than restoration. [So He is capable of restoration as He was capable of origination. The verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two complementary elements are each mentioned in one place and omitted in the other): He mentioned the return first as evidence of the origin second, and the completeness of power second as evidence of the completeness of knowledge first, because they are mutually implicated.]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verse 5:

Since the warning and the encouragement that came before had already set up the expectation that they would turn to it (i.e., to the message) and be frightened by it, and given the particular matter of turning away, it was fitting that one ask: "Did they turn towards it?" So it was said: No. [He said], clarifying that turning away inwardly is like turning away outwardly, because the inward is the foundation; emphasizing it, because it is a matter that hardly seems credible, and emphasis is more effective in rebuking them: ﴿Surely they fold their breasts﴾, that is, the disbelieving, stubborn ones, ﴿they fold their breasts﴾, meaning they bend them over and turn away from the truth with rancour, not with turning towards it, because whoever turns towards something turns to it with his chest. ﴿That they may hide from Him﴾, meaning they wish to bring about the concealment of their secret to the utmost degree. If their intention by the folding (thaniy) is concealing themselves from God Most High, then the matter of the pronoun referring to Him, glorified is He, is clear. If it is from the Prophet ﷺ, then hiding from him is hiding from the One who sent him. Then he informed that this does not avail them, because He knows their secret and their open speech, in their most hidden states in their own view, and that is the time of their covering themselves with their garments, so they cover the faces, which reveal some of what is in the hearts to those who discern (al-mutawassimin). So he said: ﴿Surely when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, meaning they bring about the act of covering them, that is, covering their heads with them, out of a desire to hide, out of aversion to hearing the words of God and the reports of His Messenger ﷺ. ﴿He knows what they conceal﴾, meaning He brings about their concealment at any time and of any kind, without delay for reflection or contemplation. [Since knowledge of the secret and of the open does not necessarily entail one another, as the open is specific to what occurs through absence or through differences in voices, wording, language, and the like, He said, explicitly]: ﴿and what they disclose﴾, meaning He brings about their disclosure, with no difference in His knowledge between concealment and disclosure, so there is no reason for their hiding out of hypocrisy, for the market of their hypocrisy is not current before Him, glorified is He. Then He gave the reason with what is more subtle than all of that, while including both kinds, and said: ﴿Surely He is All-Knowing﴾, meaning, extremely profound in knowledge, ﴿of what is in the breasts﴾, meaning the inner dispositions of their hearts which lie within their breasts, which they fold, before they came to conceive them, indeed before He created them. The root of thanaya is bending, from which come ithnan (two), because one bends toward the other, and thana' (praise), because it gathers virtues in praise. For this reason, when the servant said in al-Fatiha: ﴿the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Fatiha: 3] after the praise, God Most High said: "My servant has praised Me," as in the hadith: "I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant into two halves." And istithna' (exception) is because the second is bent back upon the first by extraction from it; and istikhfa' is seeking the hiddenness of a thing.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verse 6:

Then He followed that with what indicates the comprehensiveness of both knowledge and power together, saying: (p-237) ﴿And there is no creature﴾ and He went to the extreme of generality with His words ﴿of any moving creature﴾, and He indicated, with His words ﴿on the earth﴾, that the benefit of wealth is restricted to the people of the lower world. That is, whether it is small or large, ﴿except that upon Allah﴾, that is, upon the Sovereign King, to whom alone belongs all-encompassing reach and not upon anyone else, ﴿is its provision﴾, that is, its food and that by which it benefits and lives, in accordance with what He has made binding upon Himself, [confirming its arrival and prompting reliance upon Him in it], because bestowing favor upon every soul with that without which it cannot live and which suits it only from Him, for the duration of its life, is more precise than what has passed in knowledge, along with its including the completeness of power. The verse, along with this, also looks toward encouraging the verse ﴿And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾ [Hud: 3]. So the meaning is: devote worship sincerely to Him, and do not slacken in His worship due to being occupied with provision, for He has guaranteed it for you, and He is knowing of every soul, so do not fear that He will forget anyone.

And He said, ﴿on the earth﴾ so that it encompasses what walks upon its surface and what is within its layers of worms and the like, which none knows but Him. I have myself witnessed, inside a pebble from the shore of the Sea of Cyprus, very hard, as if it were white carnelian, a worm with food beside it; and the virtuous ʿIzz al-Din Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tukruri al-Kutubi informed me that he had witnessed, more than once, inside stones cut from the mountain of Egypt, worms having with them green grass to eat and water to drink. By His words ﴿and He knows its resting place﴾ He draws attention: that is, its place where it rests, ﴿and its repository﴾, that is, its place where it is deposited before settling, whether in a loin, a womb, or an egg, or after that, in a grave, a desert, or other than that, according to what His knowledge encompasses of the details of (p-238) the stillnesses and movements, what has occurred and what will occur of all that, which bewilders thought and astonishes minds. Then He made the closing phrase of the verse that which is of utmost greatness in the sight of the Truth, namely: ﴿all of it﴾, that is, of that, ﴿is in a clear Book﴾, for not everything the servant knows is within his power to write, nor is everything he writes so clear that whenever he wishes to uncover something from it he finds what he wants, and when he finds it, it conveys its meaning to him. The "dābba" is the living being whose nature is to crawl; the "mustaqarr" is the place in which a thing settles, its abode and place to which it returns; and the "mustawda'" is the meaning placed within its settled place, like the fetus in the womb and the drop of semen in the loin. He, glory be to Him, has placed in His Book what has been mentioned as a judgment, of which there is for the angels a lesson when compared with what occurs of written matters before their existence.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verse 7:

When the creation of that from which provision comes was greater than the creation of provision and its distribution, in the comprehensiveness of both knowledge and power, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And He is the One who created﴾, that is, alone, ﴿the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, brought into being and determined, alone, with no one sharing Him in that, as you yourselves acknowledge, ﴿in six days﴾. Since the creation of the Throne ('Arsh) is greater than all of that, for all the heavens and the earth in relation to it are like a ring thrown into a desert. And greater than that is that it should be borne upon the water, which in the ordinary course cannot be carried except in a firm and well-fitted vessel. He followed this with His saying: ﴿And His Throne was﴾ [that is] before the creation of these, ﴿upon the water﴾, being raised above it. This does not necessarily entail (p-239) contact, just as the sky is above the earth without contact. It is known from this context that there was a creation [before] the earth, so it is established that He and what is beneath Him are borne by sheer power, without any other cause, near or distant. Thereby it is established that His power is in degrees of greatness without limit. This is an additional detail to what was mentioned in Surah Yunus concerning the Throne, since this is the Surah of detail. By His saying, may He be exalted, linked to "created": ﴿that He may test you﴾, that is, [that He created all of that for you as a complete dwelling, with its cradle and its roof, with your food and drink and everything you need in it, and what benefits you and what harms you, and He empowered you over all of that], the wisdom in creating that is that He deals with you as one who tests. He indicated the intensity of this concern by framing it as a question in His saying: ﴿which of you is best in deed﴾, that is, O servants, given that He performed these tremendous acts for the sake of these matters, which you treat lightly and at which you mock. He made the verb of testing depend on the interrogative clause because it carries the meaning of knowledge, since it is the path to it. Al-Bukhari related in the Book of Tafsir from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Spend, and I shall spend upon you," and he said: "The hand of Allah is full; spending does not diminish it, it pours forth night and day." And he said: "Have you considered what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? For it has not diminished what is in (p-240) His hand. And His Throne was upon the water, and in His hand is the scale; He lowers and raises." In the verse there is an exhortation to good deeds and constant advancement in the ranks of perfection, from knowledge, which is the deed of the heart, [and the deed] of the outward action, which is the function of the limbs.

When the resurrection was established, by His hand, the creation which you [acknowledge] with [it] you acknowledge, and it was established by the test that the wisdom in creating the responsible beings is not complete except by their resurrection, so that He may recompense each of the good-doer and the evildoer for their actions [and that they were created only for that]. He marvelled at their denial of it and emphasized it for that reason, so He said: ﴿And if you say﴾, that is, to these people, whom I did not create this great creation except to test them, ﴿that you will surely be raised﴾, that is, that you will exist [your resurrection] is certain, definitely unavoidable.

When the time of the resurrection is some time, He said: ﴿after death﴾, which is at the extremity of beginning, ﴿they will surely say﴾, He emphasized it to show knowledge of the outcomes, as one of the signs of prophethood, ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, that is: ﴿this is not﴾, meaning the claim of resurrection, ﴿but manifest magic﴾, that is, a thing like magic, a false illusion with no reality, or a deception that turns people away from indulging in pleasures so that they enter into obedience to the command.

[p. 241] Since the actions of these people that preceded, and the statements they had already made, were a reason to expect that He would hasten their seizure (bil-akhdh), and since the reality is that He, Exalted is He, deals with them by granting respite out of His bounty and generosity, He relates their statement in contrast to His mercy toward them. He says: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them﴾, meaning, by Our majesty, which nothing escapes, ﴿from them﴾, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿the punishment﴾, meaning that which was threatened, ﴿until a community﴾, meaning a span of time free of turmoil, ﴿numbered﴾, meaning limited in its days, that is, short and known to Us, until breaths are counted, ﴿they will surely say﴾, repeatedly, ﴿"What is holding it back?"﴾, meaning the punishment from occurring, hastening it in mockery and denial. This is a warning to them that it will come to them soon, so let them prepare for it.

Since a sensible person should not ask about such a thing except after being able to repel it, He turned away from their response and informed them that they are powerless to repel it when it befalls them. This is to show that they had reversed matters in the question, and to confirm that what they mocked will certainly reach them. So He said, emphasizing their strong denial: ﴿Unquestionably, on the day﴾, and it is in the accusative (manṣūb) by the predicate of *laysa* (ليس), which indicates the permissibility of the predicate preceding its subject, ﴿it comes to them, it is not﴾, that is, the punishment, ﴿averted from them﴾, meaning in any way whatsoever. [And He placed the past tense (al-māḍī) in the position of the future (al-mustaqbal) for the sake of certainty and emphasis in the warning, so He said]: ﴿and there befell them﴾, meaning it overtook them at that time, encompassing them, ﴿what they used to﴾, meaning by their innate natures and evil dispositions, and He placed the adverbial complement (al-ẓarf) first to indicate the intensity of their engagement in mocking it, as if they mock nothing else, so He said: ﴿at it﴾. Since their urging for haste was itself mockery, He put in the place of "they hasten" His saying: [p. 242] ﴿they mock﴾, meaning they produce mockery of it to a great degree, as if they were seeking that.

When their saying that arose from man's natural tendency to cling to his present condition, and to be blind to being guided by the light of reason regarding what would remove it in the end, He explained this [so that it may be known that his nature is contrary to what the purpose of the surah contains of *ihkam* (firm, sound ordering), which is the fruit of knowledge. And by knowing this, one knows the measure of His blessing upon the one whom He preserved in the form in which He created him, the best of forms]. He said, emphasizing it, since every person denies that his nature is like that: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us,﴾ i.e., by what We possess of majesty, ﴿man﴾, i.e., this kind, which takes comfort in itself. Since seizing what is borrowed is among the most ugly of traits, and blessings are loans from God, Who grants them to whom He wills of His servants, He placed the relative clause first as an indication of the loan, saying: ﴿from Us, mercy,﴾ i.e., a blessing, a bounty from Us upon him, not by his own power or strength [from a direction he does not expect, by what the particle of doubt indicates], and We enabled him to enjoy it, enabling the one who tastes to taste what is tasted. ﴿Then We withdraw it from him,﴾ i.e., by what We possess of majesty, even though he dislikes that, taking back what is Our right. ﴿Indeed he is despairing,﴾ i.e., intensely hopeless that the like of it will return to him. ﴿Ungrateful,﴾ i.e., greatly concealing the favors that preceded it for him, because that is his condition and his disposition, ﴿except whom your Lord has shown mercy.﴾

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verses 10–11:**

﴿And if We let him taste comfort﴾ from Our bounty.

Since his grasping at worldly possessions is innate to him, he cannot be freed from it except by a mighty help from God. He indicated this by what it implies: that even if he remained in hardship his whole life and then attained a state he liked after a period of hardship, he would hasten to believe that this state is his original condition, that it will never leave him, that no kind of harm mixes with it, and that no trace of distress disturbs its purity. So He said, indicating the connection of the period of hardship with the statement by omitting the preposition from the adverbial noun (naz' al-khafid): ﴿after adversity﴾, that is, severe poverty harmful to his body. He did not attribute the touching of it to Himself, as He did with comfort, teaching good manners, and so He said: ﴿touches him﴾, that is, because of what his hands have earned, ﴿he will surely say﴾, despite the recent passing of adversity, out of lightness and frivolity, ﴿the evils have gone away﴾, that is, everything that troubles me, ﴿from me﴾. As for His saying ﴿Indeed he﴾, the pronoun refers to man, meaning mankind. This is a well-known universal statement (kulliyyah mashhurah) with a comprehensive subject (bi-mustaghraq), meaning that every person ﴿is exultant, boastful﴾, that is, goes beyond the limit in his joy, and is excessive in his boasting over others for every blessing God has bestowed upon him. [He does not control the harm to his own self or prevent it from himself.] Therefore the following was connected [to it], making an exception from "man," which here denotes a generic noun (ism al-jins): ﴿except those who are patient﴾ in times of hardship and the loss of blessings, hoping in their Lord and having good expectation of Him, because of their faith, which necessitates their adherence to the Law, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ [that is,] of words and actions of gratitude when blessings arrive. They are always occupied with their Lord, thankful and patient. [They are those upon whom He has perfected His blessings and created them in the best form. They are fewer than the few, because of their great struggle against their own selves (nufus) in what they have been disposed to regarding portions (hudhuz), desires, and others, and against their devils.]

Since it was as if it had been said: "Why then are they not like that?", the context yielded their praise, so He said: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the exalted in rank, ﴿for them is forgiveness﴾ if a lapse occurs from them, ﴿and a great reward﴾ for their patience and gratitude.

Note: "dhawq" (tasting) is taking a thing into the mouth to perceive its taste, just as "shamm" (smelling) is bringing a thing to the nose to perceive its scent. "Nazʿ" (removal) is lifting a thing from something else with which it was intertwined, like uprooting and peeling off. "Yaʾs" (despair) is the certainty that a thing will not happen; it is the opposite of hope. "Ya'us" (despairing) means one who despairs greatly, and this is a censure, because it stems from ignorance of the vastness of mercy, which necessitates strong hope in everything whose performance is permissible in wisdom. "Namaʾ" (comfort) is a favour whose effect appears on its recipient, just as "darraʾ" (adversity) is a harm through which one's condition becomes evident, since it is expressed in the manner of apparent conditions, as in "ḥamraʾ" and "ʿawraʾ," together with the intensification contained in its meaning. "Sayyiʾah" (evil) is what displeases from the standpoint of natural or rational aversion, and here it is illness, poverty, and the like. "Farah" (joy) is the opening of the heart with what gives pleasure. The words of al-Baghawi: it is a delight in the heart upon attaining what is desired, and it is greater than the pleasures of the senses. "Fakhr" (boasting) is haughtiness through enumerating virtues. "Sabr" (patience) is restraining [the self] from desiring what is forbidden and the like; and patience upon the bitterness of truth leads to success in the Hereafter, along with the beauty it has in this world. "Kabir" (great) is one whose measure exceeds that of others; "kathir" (many) is a plural that exceeds the number of others.

(p. 245) When Allah, glory be to Him, made an exception from those who run along with their natural dispositions and are heedless in their desires, namely the one who adorned himself with the steadfastness of patience (*sabr*) that arises from the dignity of knowledge that bears fruit in righteous action, and he (ﷺ) was the foremost of the patient, and their earlier words and deeds were like their saying, ﴿What is holding it back?﴾ [Hud: 8], and their folding their breasts as causes of the constriction of his breast (ﷺ), it might have been a cause for their hope that he (ﷺ) would leave off some of what was revealed to him about the blameworthiness of their gods, the misguidance of their forefathers, the foolishness of their judgments, and other things that grieve them, out of desire for their acceptance or fear of their turning away. For they used to say: "We do not see him mentioning those who oppose his religion, the Jews and the Christians, with the same evil he mentions us with." Allah, the Exalted, said, as a consequence of that, forbidding in the form of a statement: ﴿So perhaps you will leave out some of what***﴾ that is, out of compassion or hope, ﴿***is revealed to you***﴾. And since what was revealed had become known to them, even though they disputed it, He made the verb passive in His saying ﴿is revealed to you﴾, as in the warning and the denouncing of their forefathers' judgments, ﴿and your breast is constricted by it﴾, that is, by that part, ﴿your breast﴾, fearing that they would reject it if you conveyed it to them. Then He gave the reason for that with His saying: ﴿that﴾, that is, lest or for the sake of ﴿they say﴾ out of obstinacy and contention, since if they were seeking guidance, a single sign would have sufficed them. ﴿Why﴾, that is, why not and why is it not the case, ﴿has not a treasure been sent down to him﴾ by which he would be sufficient and free to pursue what he wants, [and He made it passive because the aim is simply its occurrence]. They used to disparage the Qur'an, knowing that it is the greatest sign, so they did not count it a sign, out of stubbornness and arrogance. ﴿Or an angel accompany him﴾, that is, to support his words and bear witness to him. So the Prophet (ﷺ) would feel constriction in his breast at such words of theirs, and it would weigh on him to deliver to them what they would not accept, and they would laugh (p. 246) at him. So Allah stirred him by this to perform the message, whatever might befall him in it. The meaning is: since it is established that man is disposed to this kind of fluctuation, do not be a target of their hope that you would leave off what angers them of what We command you [but be] among the patient. The people of the biographies (*ahl al-siyar*) said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) openly proclaimed Islam to his people and declared it as Allah had commanded him, his people did not move far from him nor did they respond to him until he mentioned their gods and reviled them. When he did that, they grew greatly angry with him, denied him, and united against him, except for those whom Allah protected. And on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "The polytheists said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Bring us a Book that contains no reviling of our gods.'"

When this context implied a denial of the wish for a halt to warning, it was as if it were said to him: this hoped-for thing is objectionable, and the greatest aim of the message is warning, for it is the hard part for souls, whereas good news can be conveyed by anyone who is able to convey it. Therefore He said: ﴿You are only a warner﴾, so convey to them what you were sent with, and they will say to you what Allah decrees for them. So do not let it grieve you [so there is upon you only the conveying], and you are not a guardian over them, by whom you could bring them back to obedience through compulsion and overpowering. Rather, the Guardian is Allah, who does what He wills. ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses complete encompassment.

Since the context concerns His encompassing, glory be to Him, He placed first His saying ﴿over all things﴾, whether concerning them or others, their acceptance or rejection, or your protection from them or from others, ﴿is Guardian﴾. [He manages affairs according to the wisdom He knows; if He wills, He brings what they asked for, and if He does not will it, He does not bring it, and there is no objection to Him.] So rely upon Him in every matter, however difficult. Perhaps He restricted the verse to warning because the situation calls for it, since they are deserving of it, and because it is what they are greedy to abandon by encouraging them to reconcile through turning away from what would cause opposition. The *ṣadr* (breast) is the seat of the heart, and the chief of a people or the one seated highest in the assembly is likened to it, for the loftiness of his rank over other people. The *kanz* (treasure) is what is buried; in religious usage it has become a term of blame for any wealth from which the obligatory *zakat* has not been paid, even if it is not buried. [This verse is an instance of *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device of mutual implication): it first negated his ability to bring what they asked for, as evidence of the ability of the One who sent him to do that and other things; and it secondly affirmed the guardianship, as evidence of its negation in the first part.]

The commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verse 13:

Since people of lofty aspirations do not aim at treasures and wealth, and since sovereignty is sought only to soothe the soul through the establishment of a matter, and since among what bears witness to the inimitability of the Qur'an, through the wondrous arrangement of its wording, its dazzling wisdom and its judgments, its awe-inspiring strangeness and abundant knowledge, is what suffices in place of that, and since in every verse of it there is what makes clear to understanding the baseness of their disparagement of the Message, it became the place of denial of it. So it was as if it were said: Do they say this out of obstinacy on their part, and a demand for proposals, and turning away from the inimitable Qur'an? Then turn away from it, for it does no harm to the direction of the proof. ﴿Or do they say﴾ [i.e., repeating], ﴿"He has invented it"﴾. So this was the place for it to be said: Yes, they indeed say this, disparaging the proof. So what is to be said to them? It was said: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., to them, by way of concession: ﴿"Then bring"﴾, O assembly of the Arabs, for you are like me in Arabic and in tongue (p-248) and in birthplace and era, and among you are those who surpass me in writing and reading, in association with scholars, in learning from the wise, in composing poetry, in producing sermons and prose, in devising proverbs, and in everything that brings nobility and pride, ﴿"with ten surahs"﴾, i.e., pieces, each piece of which encompasses a complete meaning that is argued for within it, ﴿"like it"﴾, i.e., the ten should be like the entirety of the Qur'an in its length and in its similar containing of the methods of eloquence and the varieties of sweetness, firmness, masculine vigour, and grace, while being ﴿"fabricated"﴾, i.e., you have indeed been unable to bring a single surah, meaning one piece, one verse or several verses, like it in what it has of eloquence, informing of the unseen, wisdoms, rulings, promise and threat, and parables, and you have claimed out of stubborn denial that it is fabricated and empty of wisdoms. So bring ten like it merely in eloquence, not being bound by the realities of meanings and soundness of structures. This was mentioned by al-Baghawi from al-Mubarrad, and what supports it has passed in al-Baqara at: ﴿"Then bring a surah like it"﴾ [al-Baqara: 23], from al-Jahiz and others. Abu Hayyan said: The manner of one who wishes to challenge a person is first to demand that he do similar things to what he does himself, and then, when his inability becomes clear, to say: do one example alone. End of quote. So they were first challenged with the whole Qur'an, as in His saying: ﴿"Then let them bring a statement like it"﴾ [al-Tur: 34], i.e., in its certainty and its application to events and what occurs and renews itself, one thing after another. Then, after their inability, He settled the matter by the permanence of their inability in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿"Say: If mankind and the jinn were to gather..."﴾ [al-Isra: 88] — the verse, as a rebuke to them, humiliation, and incitement and urging to that. Then they were challenged (p-249) in Surat Yunus, peace be upon him, with a single surah like the whole Qur'an, without being careful in it about the detail into surahs, lightening it for them and showing contempt for their matter. When they were unable, they were challenged with ten fabricated surahs. And when He relieved them of the restriction of truth of meaning and reality of structures, He obliged them with what He had lightened for them in Yunus of detail, and He did not leave them without the lightening, as a sign of the lowliness of their affair and the contemptibility of their position, by making it only ten. When they were unable, it was repeated in the Blessed City, on account of the People of the Book, as a challenge to them with a single surah, i.e., one piece, that being coupled with the information of the permanence of their inability in that, in His saying, may He be exalted, in al-Baqara: ﴿"But if you do not, and you will never do it"﴾ [al-Baqara: 24] — the verse. So the thing challenged with in each surah is other than the thing challenged with in the other. What has passed in Yunus and al-Baqara, and what will come in al-Isra' and al-Tur, God willing, is what completes the understanding of this station. Eloquence has three tiers: the highest of them is inimitable, and the middle and lowest are possible. The challenge occurred with the highest. This is not a command to fabricate, for it is a challenge, so it is for proving inability. His saying: ﴿"and call upon whomever you can"﴾, i.e., whom you demand to help you, and he complies. Since all ranks are beneath His rank, may He be exalted, and the Arabs acknowledge that, He said: ﴿"other than God"﴾, i.e., the Supreme King. He indicated their inability by His saying: ﴿"if you are truthful"﴾. In that there is further clarification and confirmation of the proof, for every helper other than them is beneath them in eloquence, so their inability is inability for others by way of a fortiori.

And since the lowest degree of fabrication (iftira') is a person bringing out the speech of another without knowing it, and since their inability to produce a counterpart (mu'arada) was a decisive proof that they had not reached any of His speech without knowledge, nor found an equal who could bring them its like, it was established with certainty that this Qur'an is not fabricated. Then He, exalted is He, addressed all of them, [unlike what is in Surat al-Qasas], indicating the clarity of the matter [especially regarding fabrication, to everyone], and that the polytheists had arrived, through the humiliation of rebuke by challenge time after time, and through their falsehood about themselves in that arena, round after round, at a degree of incapacity by which they could not utter even a word (bint shafah) on it: ﴿So if they do not respond to you﴾, meaning: if they do not seek to answer you and bring it about, ﴿then know﴾, O people, all of you, ﴿that it was sent down﴾, meaning: [what] the sending down of this Qur'an has occurred [only] ﴿with the knowledge of God﴾, meaning the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, in accordance with the fact that Muhammad is one of them, and custom prevents that he could, alone among all the people of the earth, come upon what his Lord has not permitted of His speech, let alone that he would be its inventor. It is also possible that the pronoun in "yastajibu" (they respond) refers to "man" (whoever) in "man istata'tum" (whomever you can), and "lakum" (to you) refers to the polytheists; and likewise in His saying "fa-'lamu" (then know) and "antum" (you). ﴿And that﴾, meaning: and know that ﴿there is no god but He﴾, for if there were with Him another god, he would have matched Him in bringing the like of His speech. In this there is a threat and a despairing that their gods could protect them from the might of God.

Since this is a decisive proof of the establishment of the Qur'an, He made His saying ﴿So will you submit?﴾ a consequence of it, encouraging and warning, meaning: will you be submitting in the most complete submission?

When the exhortation in this (passage) to steadfastness in Islam, to entering into it, and the warning against holding back from it, (made clear that) it is incumbent upon the listener to hasten to it; and since the right of the Muslim is to turn away from the world (dunya) because of the evil of its outcome; and since the greatest obstacle for the polytheists to belief was that the conditions of this world had taken hold of them, for which reason they were obstinate about the treasure, he pointed to the consequences of that with His saying: ﴿Whoever desires﴾, i.e., by his intention and his deeds, such as kindness to people and other things, ﴿the life of this world﴾, i.e., and is content with it despite its baseness compared to the Hereafter, which is lofty and noble, ﴿and its adornment﴾, so he inclines toward it because of its presence, and forgets what necessitates turning away from it, namely its perishing [and its turbidity], ﴿We will pay them in full﴾, delivering to ﴿them their deeds﴾, i.e., their recompense, ﴿therein﴾, i.e., in the world, through status, wealth, and the like, ﴿and they therein﴾, i.e., in the deeds or the world, ﴿will not be deprived﴾, i.e., nothing of their recompense in it will be diminished. As for their bodies, their souls, and their religions, they are all a loss in both abodes together. In the two sentences is an explanation of the reason the punishment is withheld from them during the period of their respite, despite the evil of their deeds.

Nazm al-Durar (al-Biqa'i), commentary on Surah 11, verse 16:

When he had explained their condition in this world, he explained their condition in the Hereafter, using the demonstrative particle of distance to indicate that they are people of distance, curse, and expulsion. In His words, as a consequence of what preceded it: ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire﴾; that is, the distant ones, the hated ones. ﴿For whom there is nothing﴾, that is: no portion of anything, ﴿in the Hereafter except the Fire﴾, that is: because of the evil of their deeds and their receiving the recompense for them in this world. ﴿And what they did therein has come to nothing﴾ [that is, it became void and corrupt], ﴿and what they used to do is in vain﴾ (p-252). That is, what they made, or their making: it was built on no foundation. Since restricting the nullification (ḥubūṭ) to the Hereafter might suggest that it is a thing in itself, He said: ﴿and is in vain﴾, that is, its nullity is established in both abodes. ﴿What they used to do﴾, that is, what they did or their doing, even though they persisted in it in the manner of one who is stamped upon by it, because it is a form with no meaning, since it was built on no foundation.

Zīnah (adornment): beautifying a thing by means of something other than itself, such as a garment, an ornament, or a manner of appearance. Tawfiyah (full payment): rendering a right in its entirety. Ḥubūṭ al-ʿamal (the nullification of a deed): its becoming void, from the saying of the Arabs, ḥabiṭa baṭnuhu, meaning his belly became corrupted by bad food.

When the proofs became clear and the evidences were raised, and the deep waves of the sea overwhelmed them, this was the occasion for rebuke against one who equates the guided with the transgressor. How can one be preferred, either by considering worldly leadership while heedless of the realities of matters, or out of obstinacy, like the one among the Jews who said to the polytheists, "You are more guided than they," so [Allah] said: ﴿Is one who has clear evidence from his Lord﴾, i.e., proof and argument, ﴿from his Lord﴾, through the insight of perception and the clarity of intellect He gave him, ﴿and he seeks the Hereafter and builds his actions on a firm foundation﴾. ﴿And there follows him﴾, i.e., follows this evidence, ﴿a witness﴾, which is the Qur'an, ﴿from Him﴾, i.e., from his Lord. Or, that proof was confirmed by the mission of an Arab Messenger, with a miraculous speech, and ''from before him'', i.e., this witness was confirming it, ﴿is the Book of Moses﴾, i.e., [also] a witness, which is the Torah, in the state of being ﴿an imam﴾, worthy of being followed, ﴿and a mercy﴾, i.e., for everyone who follows it. (p-253) Since the answer was evident, He omitted it. Its estimated meaning, and Allah knows best, is: "Is one who is upon misguidance, who seeks the world, and does acts of nobility that are not built on a sound foundation, and so will be in the abode of permanence and felicity as scattered dust, like one who is upon the evidence?" Since this one who is upon the evidence is great, and was not intended as a single specific person, He resumed the explanation with the particle of plurality, as glad tidings to this noble Prophet of the multitude of his community, saying: ﴿Those﴾, i.e., those of elevated rank, by being upon guidance from their Lord, and their guidance was confirmed by a witness from before him and a witness after him, confirming it, ﴿believe in it﴾, i.e., in this Qur'an which is the witness, and they do not ascribe the one who brought it to having fabricated it. ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it﴾, i.e., in this witness, ﴿among the factions﴾, from all groups and the people of religions alike, He equated the two groups, whether out of ignorance or obstinacy, ﴿then the Fire is his appointed place﴾, i.e., his threat, and the place of his threat, where he will burn in its blaze and suffer its bitter cold.

When the threat of the Fire had been generalized, the soul's longing for what was consequently caused became intense, so the removal of what it had borne of that by brevity drew near. The matter required the omission of the nun of "takun," so it was said: ﴿So do not be﴾, i.e., O you who are addressed as the greatest, ﴿in doubt﴾, i.e., in great doubt [and delusion] ﴿about it﴾, i.e., about the Qur'an, and do not let your chest be constricted from conveying it. Or about the promise, which is the Fire and the failure, even if We bestow favor upon the one threatened with that and grant him ease in this world. Then He gave the reason for the prohibition by His saying: ﴿Indeed, it﴾, the Qur'an (p-254) or the promise, ﴿is the truth﴾, i.e., the complete one. He increased the encouragement toward it by His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who benefits you by sending it down to you.

Since its being true was a cause for hope to attach to the faith of everyone who hears it, He said: ﴿But most of the people﴾, i.e., those who are in the realm of instability, ﴿do not believe﴾ that it is true, not because doubt penetrates it, but because of the rust upon their hearts, and they will return to the punishment prepared for them, from the One for whom the word is not changed and injustice is not ascribed to Him. The aim of this interrogative is the urging toward what the interrogative in His saying ﴿So will you submit?﴾ [Hud: 14] urged, namely turning toward the true religion, in a manner that clarifies the feebleness of the minds of the doubters and the weakness of their opinions.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verse 18:

Since the disbelievers had lied against Allah by inventing religion without any proof, and had attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ) what was fabricated, Allah, glorified is He, followed that with His saying: ﴿And who does greater wrong﴾, meaning: no one does greater wrong ﴿than one who fabricates﴾, meaning: who deliberately invents, being arrogant, ﴿against Allah﴾, meaning the Greatest King, ﴿a lie﴾, to the end of the verse. This is a place where a pronoun would have been expected. Had it been used, the sentence would have read: "They do not believe, out of wrongdoing on their part, and they are the greatest of wrongdoers." Instead, the apparent noun was used to explain what they disbelieved in, because when a judgment is attached to a description, that shows the description is its cause.

When He had shown that they are the greatest wrongdoers, He followed it with their recompense, in a resumptive sentence (isti'naf), by His saying: ﴿Those﴾, who deserve remoteness from mercy. Since the very act of being presented is frightening, He used the passive form in His saying: (p-٢٥٥) ﴿are presented﴾, [meaning] for that reason, and to indicate that they are in a state of humiliation and submit to every occurrence, so their presentation is extremely easy. ﴿Before their Lord﴾, meaning the One who showed them kindness but whom they did not thank, who knows the hidden things, so they are disgraced before Him for the blame they returned for His kindness. ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾ [repeatedly], ﴿the witnesses﴾, who are those who believed in the Books, some of which bear witness to others, referred to in His saying: ﴿And there follows it a witness from Him﴾ (Hud: 17), and the angels who recorded their deeds, and their own limbs at the time when their mouths are sealed. ﴿These are the ones﴾: the demonstrative with a near particle indicates their contemptibility. ﴿Who lied﴾, being arrogant, ﴿against their Lord﴾, in claiming a partner and a son, and in declaring things lawful and unlawful, and other things [by what His kindness and long forbearance had encompassed them with]. The use of the attribute of lordship (rubbubiyyah) is the utmost in condemning them. Thus, by this saying, their disgrace is repeated before their own kind, and before everyone who hears this speech, since nothing is further from hearts than a liar. How much more so one who dares to lie against rulers, and then against the King of kings who raised them. Everyone among the people of the standing place is awaiting His kindness and fearing His vengeance. It is as if it was said: "What is theirs after this great punishment and this disgrace?" So it was said: ﴿Behold, the curse of Allah﴾, which is the expulsion of the Greatest King and His distancing, and consider how dreadful the matter is by the mention of the Essential Name. ﴿Upon the wrongdoers﴾, so how about the greatest of wrongdoers?

Then he elaborated on their wrongdoing with His saying: ﴿Those who bar⦗from⦘ [others]﴾, meaning: they turn away themselves and prevent others ﴿from the way of﴾ (p-256) ﴿Allah﴾, i.e., the religion of [the King] to whom all perfection belongs, although He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy. ﴿And seek to make it crooked﴾, meaning: they desire for the broad, easy path of religion to be ﴿crooked﴾, by casting doubts and attacking the proofs, although it is in the utmost uprightness.

Since the focus was intensely on explaining their lying and denial, the emphasis of His saying was intensified: ﴿and they﴾, meaning: with their inner selves and outward appearances. Since their denial of the Hereafter was severe, He placed His saying ﴿of the Hereafter﴾ first and repeated the pronoun for emphasis, to specify them, to establish the utmost corruption of their inner selves, and to single them out for greater disbelief, so He said: ﴿They are disbelievers﴾, meaning: they are deeply immersed in this attribute.

"Al-'Ard" (presentation) is displaying a thing so that it is seen, for the purpose of halting at a state. "Al-Sadd" (obstruction) is prevention by means of an inciting enticement that turns one away from the matter. "Al-Bughyah" (seeking) is the pursuit of some matter, namely the desire to find a meaning in what one hopes for. "Al-'Iwaj" (crookedness) is deviation from the path of rightness; in meaning it is like "al-din" with a kasra (in the sense of crookedness in meaning), and with other things it is like "al-'awd" with a fatha, distinguishing between what is seen and what is not seen. They made the easy path for the easy and the difficult for the difficult.

Al-Bukhari related in the Book of Tafsir from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ said concerning the private conference: "The believer will be brought near to his Lord until He places His covering over him and makes him acknowledge his sins: 'Do you recognize such-and-such a sin?' He will say: 'My Lord, I recognize it, I recognize it' — twice. He will say: 'I concealed it for you in the world, and I forgive it for you today.' Then He folds up the scroll of his good deeds. As for the others, or the disbelievers, they will be called out before the heads of the witnesses: ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud: 18]."

(p-257) When He had threatened them with the matters of the Hereafter, He pointed to the demonstration of His power over that in both abodes by saying: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the far-removed from the presence of mercy, ﴿were not⦅ﷲ⦆﴾, that is, in any way whatsoever, ﴿able to escape﴾. He pointed to their incapacity by stating that they cannot reach the upper world by saying: ﴿in the earth﴾, that is, escaping — which is being beyond the reach of Allah's will — was not for them, nor was it within their power, because His power over all possibilities is of one equal degree.

When He denied their being able to escape by themselves, He denied it from the side of others, saying: ﴿And they had no﴾. Since the ranks that are below His magnificence, glorified is He, are very numerous, He made clear that they are removed from each of them by affirming the preposition, saying: ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, and He went to the extreme in negation by saying: ﴿any protectors﴾, that is, ones who would do with them what a close relative does in taking charge of their interests and shielding them from calamities. Whoever cannot defend himself while alive cannot defend himself after death. So it is as if it were said: what will be done to them? It is said: ﴿Their punishment will be doubled﴾, that is, a deed will be done to it like the deed of one who competes with another in increase; and it was put in the passive form because the emphasis is on the existence of doubling in general. ﴿For them the punishment﴾ [that is], for what they used to double of sins. Then he gave the reason for the doubling: that He created for them hearing and sight, but they wasted both through their deafness to the truth and their blindness to it. So it is as if there were no difference between them and one who lacks them, and so He said: ﴿They were not﴾, that is, by what was in them of corruption of natures (p-258) ﴿able to hear﴾, that is, they were capable, in view of their original sound natures, which had been overcome by their submission to desire and their taking on the defects of appetites, so that His obedience would exist in them; so they did not hear. ﴿Nor were they﴾ able to see, so they ﴿did not see﴾ until they turn away from appetites, whereupon their ability to hear [and see] would exist. This is a metonymy for their non-acceptance of the truth, and that the intensity of their aversion from it reached a limit at which they are described as lacking the ability, just as a person says, when his aversion to something is intense: "This is something I cannot bear to hear." The doubling is by disbelief and obstruction. Negating ability is more emphatic in censure, more indicative of deficiency, and more painful than negating hearing, because they may take it as a refusal to respond. As for negating sight, it is inseparable from deficiency, whether of the eye or of the heart. This holds if the verse is not construed as ihtibak; if it is so construed, the two matters are equal, and the negation of ability first indicates its negation second, and the negation of sight indicates the negation of hearing first.

When it was established that they have no hearing and no sight, it was established that they are nothing at all. So He said: ﴿Those are they﴾, that is, the remote and the hateful, ﴿who have lost their souls﴾, that is, by squandering the original nature (fitrah), which is the ease of submitting to good and the difficulty of submitting to evil. And since the helpless person may be benefited by one who serves him, gaining him strength after weakness and vigor after incapacity, He negated that by His saying, returning to the negation of benefit from those whom He had first excused, in the best manner: ﴿And what they used to fabricate has forsaken them﴾, that is, the state they were created upon, so that they could not be detached from it, ﴿fabricate﴾, that is, they deliberately lied when they claimed that they were gods. There is no doubt that whoever has lost his soul, and whoever has lost it on their account by claiming that they are partners of its Creator and the like, is the greatest of people in loss. Therefore He said: ﴿Undoubtedly﴾, that is, without doubt, ﴿that they﴾, that is, these who went to extremes in denying the Hereafter, ﴿in the Hereafter﴾. Since the situation called for emphasis in describing them with loss, He repeated the pronoun and said: ﴿they are﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿the greatest losers﴾, that is, the most lost of all who can be described as losers. 

The i'jaz (inability to bring about the thing) is: the impossibility of the object of an act, such that its occurrence is not possible. The mudā'afah (multiplication) is: an increase over a quantity by its equivalent or more. The istiṭā'ah (capacity) is: a power by which the limbs are made obedient to the act.

As for ﴿lā jaram﴾, the scholars of Arabic have differed in interpreting it. Al-Raḍī said in his commentary on al-Ḥājibiyyah, and al-Safāqisī in his al-Burhān on its i'rab (grammatical analysis), in summary: the common usage after lā jaram is the fatḥah, that is, on ﴿anna﴾. Then lā is either a rejection of the preceding speech, according to the view of al-Khalīl, or it is extra, as in lā uqsimu, because in jaram there is the meaning of an oath. It is a past-tense verb according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl, compounded with lā. Sībawayh made it a verb meaning ḥaqqa (it is true), with anna as its subject. It has been said: jaram in the meaning of ḥaqqa, and it is the subject of lā, and annahum is its predicate. Al-Kisā'ī said: its meaning is: no hindrance and no prevention. From al-Zajjāj: it is not compounded, and there is no negation of what has been said, that they have idols that benefit them. Jaram is a past-tense verb meaning kasaba (he earned), its subject is an implied pronoun referring to their act, and innahum is its object. Al-Farrā' said: it is a word originally meaning lā budda (there is no escape) and lā maḥālah (there is no doubt), for he transmits from the Arabs lā jurm, meaning with a ḍammah then a sukūn, and the verb, meaning in this manner, and the verb, meaning vowelled, both share in the verbal nouns like al-rushd, al-ra'd, and al-bukhl. Al-jaram is cutting, that is, there is no cutting from this, just as lā budda means there is no cutting. It became common and took this course until it came to have the meaning of an oath, so it is answered with what an oath is answered with. It is said: lā jaram la-ātiyannaka (there is no doubt I will surely come to you), and lā jaram annaka qā'im (there is no doubt that you are standing). Whoever reads it with fatḥah does so in view of the original form of lā jaram, as we say: lā budda an naf'ala kadhā wa-annaka taf'alu, that is, from an and from annaka taf'alu. Whoever reads it with kasrah does so for the meaning of the oath that has arisen in lā jaram. End of quotation.

So his interpretation of it as cutting is considered, in that the root jaram specifically revolves around cutting. The more appropriate interpretation is as doubt, in view of what the root itself revolves around, in whatever order it occurs: jaram, [jamar], rajam, ramaj, majar, and maraj. I have made it so because they said: jaram al-nakhl meant he estimated its yield, and ajmara al-nakhl also meant he estimated its yield; rajama meant when he supposed; al-majar is the intellect, and suspicion entails the kindling of the mind, from which comes jamrat al-nār (ember of fire); al-jarm for the hard ground that is strongly pulled; suspicion also entails the gathering of thought, from which comes al-jamrah for the heart and everything resembling it in gathering; from it comes al-jirm (with kasrah), which is the body, for it is considered in terms of its whole; and the voice, or its loudness, for the throat is gathered in it for cutting; gathering also entails greatness, from which comes ajrama, meaning he became great; al-jamīr, like amīr, is the gathering place of a people; from gathering comes ostentation and intellect, from which clarity arises; from it comes ﴿a flame of fire﴾ [al-Raḥmān 55:15], that is, there is no smoke in it; from it comes ajrama lawnuhu, meaning its color became clear; from gathering comes al-majar (with fatḥah), which is when one fills his belly with water without being satisfied; and earning: jaram li-ahlihi, meaning he earned for his family; from it comes al-dhanb (sin), for it is a specific kind of earning; and it is possible that it is from cutting, because it cuts its doer off from good. Gathering also entails concealment, from which comes ajamarat al-laylah, meaning the crescent was hidden in it. Al-majar is for what is in the bellies of pregnant camels and goats; or this may be considered among what entails the very nature of suspicion, from obscurity. From gathering comes emaciation: ajmara al-khayl means he trained the horses by lean feeding, and shāh mujmarah means a lean sheep. Gathering also entails firmness and completeness, from which comes ḥawl mujram, like mu'ẓam, meaning complete year, from which separation arises. From it comes tajarrama al-layl, meaning the night departed; and ibnā jamīr, like amīr, are the night and the day; or this may be one of the necessary consequences of cutting, as will come. From gathering also comes al-rajm, which is the close friend and companion. Suspicion entails distinguishing between things. From it comes jirām al-nakhl, for its cutting of the dates. Al-jamrah is the pebble, so this entails throwing in general, from which arises throwing the stones (al-jimār), which are stones, from which arises killing the one stoned. This also returns to the very nature of cutting, for it is the cutting of the self from what it was upon. Distinction entails slander and blame. Al-rimāj, like saḥāb, is the knuckles of the spear, due to the separation of some of them from others. Al-ramaj with fatḥah is the bird dropping its dung. Suspicion [entails exaggeration in looking, so exaggeration appears in speech and resolve, from which comes al-mirjām for the camel that extends its neck while traveling; and ajmara means he hastened in travel; and suspicion may entail bewilderment]. From it comes a ḥadīth mujram, like mu'ẓam, meaning one whose reality cannot be grasped. Then sin, corruption, anxiety, and turmoil necessarily follow. From it comes amraja al-'ahd, meaning he did not fulfill the covenant, that is, he made it shaky and unsteady. The root maraja, in this particular arrangement, revolves around turmoil, or al-tarmīj is spoiling lines after they have been written. Suspicion entails confusion, from which comes al-jirm for color, because it is never free of admixture; ajrama al-dam bihi means it stuck to it. Al-ijrām is the herdsman's goods, or it is from earning. Al-jurrām, like rummān, is fish. Al-maraj is the grazing place. It is known from this that all forms of the root revolve around turmoil, and this is clear in everything except the intellect. As for the intellect, it is considered as turmoil of opinion, because the intelligent person, whenever he examines carefully, has opened to him what was closed, so he turns toward it. When this is clear, it becomes evident that the meaning of lā jaram is: there is no suspicion and no turmoil regarding the fact that they [annahum]. The negation of suspicion in such a context is the negation of everything opposed to it, except the knowledge that is in the sense of certainty, just as when one says: there is no doubt in such and such and no uncertainty. It is thus clarified that their interpretation of it as "truly" is an interpretation of meaning for the two words combined. For when suspicion is negated in such a context, certainty and conviction are established. To this returns Sībawayh's interpretation as "no right," for he means, God knows best, that it is not a connective particle (ṣilah), and its original function is negation. It negates the opposite of what it enters upon. So it is as if it were said: it is true and established that they are such and such, and everything opposed to it is negated. This is the way in which it is an emphatic connective. Similar to this is what has been said about innamā, as in: innamā Zayd qā'im, meaning: Zayd is standing, and nothing else is the case. Thus it has become clear that the negating particle, in the same way, is emphatic. And God is the Granter of success.

When it was established that they have no hearing and no sight, it was established that they are nothing at all. So He said: ﴿Those are they﴾, that is, the remote and the hateful, ﴿who have lost their souls﴾, that is, by squandering the original nature (fitrah), which is the ease of submitting to good and the difficulty of submitting to evil. And since the helpless person may be benefited by one who serves him, gaining him strength after weakness and vigor after incapacity, He negated that by His saying, returning to the negation of benefit from those whom He had first excused, in the best manner: ﴿And what they used to fabricate has forsaken them﴾, that is, the state they were created upon, so that they could not be detached from it, ﴿fabricate﴾, that is, they deliberately lied when they claimed that they were gods. There is no doubt that whoever has lost his soul, and whoever has lost it on their account by claiming that they are partners of its Creator and the like, is the greatest of people in loss. Therefore He said: ﴿Undoubtedly﴾, that is, without doubt, ﴿that they﴾, that is, these who went to extremes in denying the Hereafter, ﴿in the Hereafter﴾. Since the situation called for emphasis in describing them with loss, He repeated the pronoun and said: ﴿they are﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿the greatest losers﴾, that is, the most lost of all who can be described as losers.
