(p-287) When the command came to him concerning this, he hastened to obey, and he gathered those whom God had commanded him to take into the ship, after he had readied it for them. ﴿And he said﴾, that is, to those who had been commanded to be carried: ﴿Embark in it﴾. Since the sense of place ("in") is more prevalent with regard to a ship, he said ﴿in it﴾, that is, in the ship. When he had commanded them to board and they boarded, he resumed his speech; or, he commanded them to board, saying: ﴿In the name of God﴾, that is, the One who has complete encompassing power, ﴿its course and its anchorage﴾, that is, its sailing and its mooring, and the place and time of each. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Humayd al-A'raj and Isma'il ibn Mujalid, from 'Asim, read it with a pure kasra on the ra' and the sin, followed by two pure ya's, on the basis that the two nouns are descriptive attributes of the Divine Name (al-Jalalah). Then he gave the reason for their deliverance by its sailing and mooring, acknowledging that there is no deliverance except by His pardon, with his words: ﴿Indeed, my Lord﴾, that is, the One who has been good to me by ordering this matter for me and other things. He increased the emphasis, as a means of comforting the hearts of those with him, informing them that no one will truly measure God by His due measure, and that the servant cannot but seek forgiveness; so He said: ﴿is indeed All-Forgiving﴾, that is, exceedingly concealing of lapses and failings, ﴿All-Merciful﴾, that is, exceedingly bountiful toward whomever He wills. So they boarded it and continued sailing in it, saying: "In the name of God."

"And it" — that is, while the state was that it ﴿was running with them﴾

Since water is by nature prepared for drowning, sailing upon its surface was one of the extraordinary things, and He indicated this by the adverbial phrase, saying: ﴿in waves﴾. He drew attention to its height by His saying: ﴿like mountains﴾, meaning: in their magnitude, their piling up [and their height]. The clause is thus a circumstantial clause (hal) from the implied ﴿they boarded it﴾, because the implied element is as strong as the stated one by virtue of its being evident. This state, along with the fact that continuing to ride is itself a form of riding, is an indication of the swiftness with which the earth filled with water and it became like mountains, immediately after they boarded the ship, without significant delay. They said: the first to board with him was the ant, and the last to board with him was the donkey. Iblis clung to its tail and could not enter until Noah, peace be upon him, said to him: "Enter, even if the devil is with you." Thus they said. It was also said that he prevented the snake and the scorpion, saying: "You two are the cause of harm." They said: "Carry us, and we promise not to harm anyone who mentions you." Therefore whoever says: ﴿Peace be upon Noah among the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 79] ﴿Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good﴾ [al-Saffat: 80] ﴿Indeed, he was among Our believing servants﴾ [al-Saffat: 81], they will not harm him.

Since the beginning of the state was the gushing forth of the whole earth in springs and the pouring of the sky in torrents, this indicates that the state would reach what Allah informed of, namely that the waves would be like mountains, from which nothing saves except the means that He, glory be to Him, had established. He followed that with the matter of Noah's son, saying, conjoining it to His saying: ﴿And he said, "Board it"﴾ [Hud: 41]: ﴿And Noah called to his son﴾ — [namely] Kan'an, and he was of his loins; al-Rummani transmitted this from Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak. ﴿And he was in a separate place﴾, meaning: apart from his father, in his place and in his religion, because he was a disbeliever. He made clear that this separation was at some distance by His saying: ﴿O my little son﴾ — He diminutized it out of tenderness and affection — ﴿Board with us﴾, being present ﴿with us﴾, that is, in the ship, so that you may be among the saved, ﴿and do not be﴾, meaning: in no way whatsoever, ﴿with the disbelievers﴾, meaning: in religion or in place. This indicates that the zeal and compassion of the messengers, peace be upon them, even amid witnessing great signs and awesome events, are not a cause for softening hearts and subduing souls unless Allah permits. Observe Noah's pleading appeal, peace be upon him, in his saying: "O my little son," reminding him of prophethood, together with the diminutive of tenderness and compassion, while the son's harshness persisted, as he would not allow himself to say "O my father," and he did not soften despite the great signs he had seen, nor did he desist from any of them from rushing into ignorance instead of knowledge and from arbitrary doubt instead of proof.

When the situation was one of bewilderment and disorder, the listener was likely to be impatient and to hasten to ask, "So what did he say?" Therefore it is said: ﴿He said﴾, speaking as one who lacks understanding, in accordance with what God intended: ﴿"I will betake myself to a mountain that will protect me﴾, meaning by its height, ﴿from the water,﴾ meaning so that I will not drown. ﴿He said﴾, meaning Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿"There is no protector﴾, meaning there is no preventer, neither mountain nor anything else, existing ﴿today from the command of God,﴾ meaning for anyone, ﴿the Sovereign, the Greatest, whose command, power and knowledge encompass all things,﴾ namely His judgment that every living creature [that lives in water] be drowned, ﴿except for him on whom He has mercy.﴾ meaning except for a place of God's mercy, which is a preventer from that, namely the ship; or rather, whoever God has mercy upon, God will protect him."

When Noah and those whom God commanded him to take aboard had boarded, and He willed it, and there was no further need for the gradual rising of the water, it rose, swelled, overpowered and became violent, so the matter became terrifying and exceeded its limit and measure. [God, may He be exalted, said, linking this to what is implied: his son did not heed this from him, but disobeyed his father just as he had disobeyed God, and took refuge in the mountain he had chosen, so the water rose over him, and afterward it was no longer possible for him to catch up with his father or reach him.] ﴿And the wave came between them,﴾ meaning between the son and the mountain, or between him and his father, ﴿the wave﴾ mentioned in His words: ﴿in waves like mountains﴾ [Hud: 42]. ﴿So he was among the drowned,﴾ meaning [the son] was among those who were destroyed with the least difficulty, and they are all those on earth who did not board with Noah, peace be upon him.

Abu Hayyan said: It was said that they were exchanging words, but before the exchange was completed, a great wave came. He was riding a horse that had become arrogant and self-admiring, so the wave swallowed him and his horse, and he was cut off from Noah, peace be upon him, and drowned. End of quote.

Riding (rukub) means being raised upon the back of a thing: one rides an animal, a ship, the land or the sea. Flowing (jary) means swift passage; one says, "This cause flows in its rulings," meaning it passes through without any impediment. Waves (mawj) is the plural of mawjah, a great portion of abundant water that rises from its mass, and this is greatest when the wind becomes violent. A mountain (jabal) is a body of great thickness that stands out from the earth and is to it like a peg. Protection (ʿisma) is safeguarding from calamity.

[p. 290]

[p. 291] **﴿And it was said﴾**, i.e., with the slightest indication, after the people of the earth had perished and it was emptied of the disbelievers, and after those among the plains and mountains who were lost had been destroyed. This is a case of using the *musabbab* (the effect), which is "saying," for the *sabab* (the cause), which is "willing," in order to depict a command and a commanded thing that are in the utmost state of obedience, for this is more striking to the soul.

Since everything below the station of majesty, grandeur and might is [only] by a command that none knows except Allah, He indicated this with the particle of distance, saying: **﴿O earth, swallow your water﴾**, i.e., draw it in without chewing, into a hidden place, gradually. He specified what is to be swallowed so that it would not be general, lest it swallow everything on its surface, such as mountains and other things. For this reason it is singular and not plural, and He said: **﴿your water﴾**, i.e., that which has gushed forth upon your surface, for the flooding, so that it would be like nourishment for the eater who strengthens his body, and thereby becomes able to produce growth and all other benefits. He made it "her water" because of its connection to her, the connection of ownership to the owner. **﴿And O sky, withhold﴾**, i.e., stop from raining. So both obeyed promptly the command of the King, from whose will nothing departs. **﴿And the water subsided﴾**, i.e., the known water was judged to be sunk into the depths of the earth. It is from the transitive form, for it is said: *ghāḍa al-māʾu* (the water subsided) and *ghāḍahu Allāh* (Allah caused it to subside), just as it is said: *naqaḍa al-shayʾ* (the thing collapsed) and *naqaḍtuhu anā* (I collapsed it). **﴿And the matter was decided﴾**, i.e., it was completed, cut off and settled, regarding the destruction of those who were destroyed and the salvation of those who were saved, as the Majestic One willed, in accordance with what His promise to Noah, peace be upon him, had preceded. No one could hold it back from them, nor turn it away, nor delay it by a moment or less. So let whoever has been spared the punishment praise Allah, and let him not say, "What holds it back?", lest there come upon him the like of what came upon these people or those after them. **﴿And it came to rest﴾**, i.e., the ship settled and became level **﴿upon al-Judiyy﴾**, indicating by its name that the general retribution had passed, and that nothing remained but the bounty of water, goodness, abundance and general mercy. It is a mountain near Mosul, reached after five months. Qatadah said: they set out with them on the tenth of Rajab, and they were on the water for one hundred and fifty days, then it settled with them on al-Judiyy for a month, and they descended on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. **﴿And it was said﴾**, i.e., as an announcement of the humiliation of those who were destroyed and of the relief from them, **﴿Away with﴾**: it is from *baʿida* (to be far), with a kasra, meaning distance in terms of destruction, for its reality is a far distance from which there is no hope of return. It was then borrowed for destruction and was restricted to the invocation of evil. He expressed it with the verbal noun because it is connected with the *lām* that indicates entitlement and specificity. **﴿for the people﴾** [i.e., those known in this story, in which there was, in the severity of their opposition, what none knows except Allah] **﴿who are wrongdoers﴾**, i.e., those who were deeply immersed in wrongdoing.

This verse has nineteen words, containing twenty-one kinds of *badīʿ* (rhetorical embellishment). Abū Ḥayyān counted them, and said: It is related that a Bedouin heard it and said: "This is the speech of those who are capable." Al-Rummānī mentioned several of its meanings, among them: the issuing of the command in a manner that magnifies its doer without effort or fatigue; and among them: the fine opposition of meanings; and among them: the fine harmony of words; and among them: the excellence of expression in depicting the situation; and among them: brevity without deficiency; and among them: the ready acceptance of understanding in its utmost perfection. *Al-balʿ* (swallowing) is passing a thing through the throat into the belly. *Al-iqlāʿ* (withholding) is removing a thing from its root so that no trace of it remains. *Al-ghayḍ* (subsiding) is the disappearance of water into the earth by way of absorption. The expression of the speech in the passive form is more indicative of the majesty and greatness of the doer, to point out that he is known, since none other is capable of such acts. Al-Iṣfahānī transmitted from the author of *al-Miftāḥ* concerning it a statement more precious than jewels.

(p-294) Since the exception concerning his family in His words, ﴿except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ [Hud: 40], could be understood to refer only to his wife, the salvation of his son would be permissible. The prophets, peace be upon them, have such deep compassion for creation, especially their relatives, that it drives them to strive for their righteousness, even when there is no justification for it, as has already been explained. A similar case is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 80]. This is because the wings of created beings are broken, their hands are short, their authority is weak, and their condition is decayed. Any slight humiliation leads them to loss. But the Presence of the Truth is vast, His affair is great, and His command is exalted. No deficiency reaches Him in any way, no harm approaches Him, and no weakness affects His command. Since this is the case, Noah, peace be upon him, asked for the salvation of his son, as Allah, Exalted is He, reported about him in His words: ﴿And Noah called out to his Lord﴾ [i.e., the One who had accustomed him to abundant kindness]. By using the conjunction "fa" (then) rather than beginning a new sentence explaining the calling out, He indicated that what is mentioned here is part of Noah's calling out, and that what is mentioned here is ordered and follows upon something of his calling that came before it. The closest possibility is what He guided him to in Surat al-Mu'minun, which is hinted at by His words after this, in response to him: ﴿O Noah, descend with peace from Us﴾ [Hud: 48]. Thus the sense of the discourse is: he said, "My Lord, cause me to land at a blessed place," and what is implied in the speech is ﴿So he said﴾, meaning: as a consequence of what moved him to that, namely the mercy of prophethood, the compassion of fatherhood, and human nature, exposing himself to the breezes of mercy and the impulses of pardon. Alternatively, the "fa" is an elaboration of the general "called out," like [in]: he performed ablution, then washed.

﴿My Lord, indeed my son﴾, meaning the one who drowned, ﴿is of my family﴾, meaning: You had commanded me to carry my family, and that command could imply an intention to save them. ﴿And indeed Your promise is the truth﴾, meaning: perfect in their salvation, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and You have known this about the disbelieving wife. ﴿And You are the most just of judges﴾, because You are the most knowing of them, and whoever is most knowing is most judicious. So You know that Your statement, ﴿except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ [Hud: 40], is valid when it excepts her alone. So if my son is among those who were saved, then bring him to me. And if this supplication was made while the waves were coming between them, then the meaning is: do not destroy him.

He said, "O Noah, he is not of your family," and he emphasized the negation of what preceded by affirming it: **﴿He is not of your family﴾**, meaning the one whose people were judged for salvation by virtue of their faith, while he is an unbeliever. For this reason the verdict is justified by his words: **﴿He is [ʿamal] ghayr ṣāliḥ﴾**. That is, he is one possessing [ʿamal] (deeds), but he has made him the very essence of deed (ʿamal) in the reading of the majority (qirāʾat al-jamāʿa, the standard recitation), as an intensification of condemning him. This is because substances are equal in their basic existence and are not distinguished except by their effects. So he made clear that there is no righteous effect in him at all. The reading of Yaʿqūb and al-Kisāʾī, with the verb (fiʿl), confirms that whoever engages in evil in any kind of engagement, disassociation from him becomes obligatory, especially for the command (al-amr), so that one does not keep company with him except by permission. He expressed it with ʿamal rather than fiʿl because he claims that his deeds are built on knowledge, and he emphasized it because of what Noah, peace be upon him, is not singled out for in this question.

**﴿unrighteous﴾** according to My knowledge. I have decided in this matter that I will not save from it except those who are characterized by righteousness, and I am All-Knowing of what is in the breasts. You do not know many matters, so you may suppose faith in one who is not a believer, because you base the matter on what we see of its outward appearance. Al-Rummānī reported from al-Ḥasan that he used to be a hypocrite by displaying faith. This indicates that one who agrees in religion is closest, even if he is at the greatest distance in lineage, and one who opposes in it is furthest, even if he is at the closest proximity in lineage.

When this answer had the consequence that abandoning the question was better, he mentioned a general principle that encompasses it, saying: **﴿So do not ask Me﴾**, that is, with any kind of asking, **﴿about that of which you have no knowledge﴾**, so you do not know whether the question about it is correct or not. This is because what befits those like you among the close kin is to base their affairs on verification and to await information from Us. Consider the words of Mūsā, peace be upon him, in the hadith of intercession in the Ṣaḥīḥ from the hadith of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him: "**And indeed I have killed a soul for which I was not commanded to kill it.**" It is known that that soul was a disbeliever from the family of Pharaoh. **﴿I admonish you﴾** with My admonitions, out of dislike that you should **﴿be﴾**, that is, a state you would take on in character, **﴿among the ignorant﴾**, that is, among those who act on assumption, because they have no way to reach the realities of matters from Our side, so you would ask as they ask.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verses 47–48 (part 1 of 2):

When it became clear to the listener what the status of the Prophet (ﷺ) was—his exalted rank and great station, which called for reproach over many a correct action—so that he yearned for the answer, the reply was resumed with his words: ﴿He said﴾, that is, hastening to it, in keeping with what the perfection of his qualities requires of him. ﴿My Lord﴾, that is, O You who have been good to me. He emphasised, to show the listeners his great desire, and said: ﴿I seek refuge in You from asking You﴾, that is, from ﴿asking You﴾ [i.e., about] any matter whatsoever ﴿of which I have no knowledge﴾, out of good manners in accepting Your permission, taking heed of Your admonition, and aspiring to what You have raised me to of high rank and lofty station. ﴿And if You do not forgive me﴾, that is, now and in the future, ﴿and have mercy on me﴾, that is, conceal my slips, erase them, and honour me, ﴿I will be among the losers﴾, that is, those who are deeply immersed in loss. So it was as if it was said: What was his answer to that? It was said: ﴿It was said﴾, in the passive form, indicating the majesty and grandeur by which great matters are accomplished with the slightest indication: ﴿O Noah, descend﴾, that is, from the ark, ﴿with peace﴾, that is, a great peace, ﴿from Us﴾, that is, and upon those with whom We have made peace, so no destruction will befall them, ﴿and blessings﴾, that is, abundant, great, and righteous goods, ﴿upon you﴾, that is, specifically for you, ﴿and upon nations﴾ arising ﴿from those with you﴾, because they are upon what pleases Us; We will not let them enjoy the world except for a little, and for them, when they return to Us, is lasting bliss. This statement includes every believing man and woman until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And [other] nations﴾, that is, from among them, ﴿We will let them enjoy [life] for a while﴾ in the world, with abundance of provision and ease of living, according to Our knowledge and will, but there will be no blessings upon them from Us, nor peace. So the verse is of the type of *ihtibak* (interlocking omission): he mentioned the blessings and peace first, as an indication of their negation the second time, and the enjoyment second, as an indication of its omission the first time. ﴿Then a painful punishment will touch them from Us﴾, that is, in both abodes, or in the Hereafter, or in both, ﴿because they persisted in other than Our guidance and dared to do what angers Us.

It is permissible that ﴿and [other] nations﴾ be a subject (mubtada') without an omitted qualifying adjective being estimated, in which case what justifies beginning with an indefinite noun is that the context is one of favour (maqam al-tafdil).

*Al-'iyadh* (seeking refuge): seeking deliverance by means of that which prevents evil. *Al-barakah* (blessing): the establishment of good that grows continuously, state after state; its root meaning is permanence, and from it come *al-buruk* (kneeling of a camel) and *al-barakah* (a pool), because water settles in it.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verses 47–48 (part 2 of 2):**

The account of Noah (peace be upon him) from the Torah. He is Noah son of Lamech, son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Cainan, son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam (peace be upon him). This is in the early part of the first book of it: "Adam knew his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and she named him Seth, and said: 'God has appointed me another offspring instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.' " This was after Adam had lived one hundred and thirty years. The total life of Adam was nine hundred and thirty years. Seth lived one hundred and five years and begot Enosh. The total life of Seth was nine hundred and twelve years. Enosh lived ninety years and begot Cainan. The total life of Enosh was nine hundred and five years. Cainan lived seventy years and begot Mahalalel. The total life of Cainan was nine hundred and ten years. Mahalalel lived sixty-five years and begot Jared. The total life of Mahalalel was eight hundred and ninety-five years. Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years and begot Enoch. The total life of Jared was nine hundred and sixty-two years. Enoch lived sixty-five years and begot Methuselah. The total life of Enoch was three hundred and sixty-five years. Methuselah lived one hundred and eighty-seven years and begot Lamech. The total life of Methuselah was nine hundred and sixty-nine years. Lamech lived one hundred and eighty-two years and had a son, and he named him Noah, saying: "This one will give us rest from our work and from the toil of our hands on the ground which the Lord has cursed." The total days of the life of Lamech were seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died. Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah begot sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth. When men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them, the sons of the nobles saw the daughters of the common people, that they were very beautiful, and they took for themselves wives from among them, whomever they chose and loved. God then said: "My care and compassion shall no longer be for these people, because they follow the desires of the body and the flesh." There were giants on the earth in those days and afterwards, because the sons of the nobles went in to the daughters of the common people, and they bore them mighty men who were famous. The Lord saw that the evil of men had multiplied on the earth, and that the inclination of their thoughts and their malice was wicked all the days. The Lord said: "I will blot out the people whom I have created from the face of the new earth, both men and beasts, and even the creeping things and the birds of heaven." But Noah found favor with God and mercy and kindness. Noah was a righteous man, pious in his generation, and he pleased God. The earth was corrupt before God and filled with wickedness and debauchery. The Lord God saw that the earth had become corrupt, and God said to Noah: "The end of all people has come before Me, and the evil of their deeds, because the earth has been filled with wickedness and debauchery through their evil conduct. Behold, I am going to destroy them along with the earth. Make for yourself an ark of square timber, of gopher wood (in another copy: cypress), and make cells in the ark, and coat it with pitch inside and out. The length of the ship shall be three hundred cubits, its breadth fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits. Make a window in the ark, and its width at the top shall be one cubit. Place the door of the ark in its side, and make it with lower, middle and upper decks. Behold, I am going to bring a flood of waters upon the earth to destroy under heaven all flesh in which is the breath of life, and everything that is on the earth will perish. But I will establish My covenant with you. You shall enter the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you. And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort, you shall bring into the ark to keep them alive with you; they shall be male and female. Of the birds according to their kinds, and of the animals according to their kinds, and of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind, two of every sort shall come to you to keep them alive. Take with you of every kind, two by two, to keep them alive, male and female. Also take with you of every food that is eaten, and store it up, and it shall be food for you and for them." Noah did everything just as God commanded him. Then God said to Noah: "Enter, you and all your household, into the ark, for I have found you righteous and pious in this generation. Of every clean animal take with you seven pairs, male and female, and of the animals that are not clean take with you two, male and female. Of the clean birds, seven pairs, male and female, and of the birds that are not clean, two by two, male and female, so that offspring may live on the face of the earth. For in seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will blot out every living thing that I have made from the face of the earth." Noah did as the Lord God commanded him. When seven days after that had passed, the waters of the flood came upon the earth. The fountains of the great deep burst forth and the windows of heaven were opened. The rain fell on the earth for forty days and forty nights. On that very day Noah and Shem, Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah's wife and the wives of his three sons, entered the ark with him, they and all the wild animals according to their kinds, and all the cattle according to their kinds, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth according to its kind, and all the birds according to their kinds. There went into the ark with Noah, from every sparrow and from every winged creature, two by two, and from every creature of flesh in which is the spirit of life, two by two. Those that went in, of all flesh, went in male and female, as God had commanded Noah. Then the Lord God shut him in. The flood was on the earth forty days and forty nights. The waters increased and lifted up the ark, and it rose high above the earth. The waters grew very deep and increased greatly on the earth, [and the ark floated upon the face of the waters, and the waters prevailed very greatly upon the face of the earth, very greatly]. All the high and lofty mountains under heaven were covered. The waters rose fifteen cubits above the mountains. Every creature of flesh that was on the earth perished, birds, wild animals, cattle, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, and all mankind. Everything on the dry land in whose nostrils was the breath of life died. Noah and those with him in the ark remained, and the waters prevailed on the earth for one hundred and fifty days. God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and cattle and all the birds that were with him in the ark. God caused a wind to blow over the earth, and the waters subsided and the rain stopped. The fountains of the deep and the windows of heaven were closed. The waters receded after one hundred and fifty days. The ark rested, and on the seventeenth day of the seventh month it settled on the mountains of Qudi. The waters continued to recede and decrease until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains appeared. After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark and sent out the raven, and it went out and kept going back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth. [Then he sent out the dove after it to see whether the waters had lessened on the face of the earth.] But the dove found no place to set her foot, so she returned to the ark, for the waters were still on the face of the earth. He put out his hand, took her, and brought her into the ark, and waited seven more days. Then he sent out the dove again, and she came back to him toward evening, and in her beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters had subsided from the earth. He waited seven more days, and sent out the dove, and she did not return to him again. Then Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and behold, the surface of the ground was dry. God spoke to Noah and said to him: "Go out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons' wives with you, and all the wild animals that are with you, of all flesh, the birds and the cattle, and bring out every creeping thing that creeps on the earth with you, that they may breed abundantly on the earth and be fruitful and multiply on the earth." So Noah went out with those mentioned, and he built an altar to the Lord and took of all the clean cattle and birds and offered burnt offerings on the altar to the Lord God. The Lord God said: "I will never again curse the ground because of man, for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth. Nor will I again destroy every living thing as I have done. As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, shall not cease." God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them: "Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth. Let the fear and dread of you fall upon all the wild animals of the earth, all the birds of the heavens, every creature that creeps on the ground, and all the fish of the sea; into your hand they are delivered. Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you; I give you all things, as I gave you the green plants. But you shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood. Surely for your lifeblood I will require a reckoning: from every beast I will require it, and from man, from every man's brother, I will require the life of man. Whoever sheds man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God He made man. And you, be fruitful and multiply, increase abundantly on the earth and multiply in it." God said to Noah and his sons with him: "Behold, I establish My covenant with you and with your descendants after you, and with every living creature that is with you, the birds, the cattle, and every wild animal of the earth with you, all that came out of the ark. I establish My covenant with you: never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, nor shall there again be a flood to destroy the earth." God said to Noah: "This is the sign of the covenant which I am making between Me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all future generations. I have set My bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth. When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow appears in the clouds, I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and never again shall the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh." The sons of Noah who went out of the ark with him were Shem, Ham and Japheth. [Ham was the father of Canaan.] These three were the sons of Noah, and from them the people were scattered over all the earth. Then it is mentioned that Noah (peace be upon him) slept, and Ham saw his nakedness and told his two brothers. Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it on their shoulders, walked backward, and covered their father's nakedness. When Noah learned what his youngest son had done, he cursed him, saying that he would be a servant to his brothers. The total days of Noah's life were nine hundred and fifty years. Then he died, peace, blessings, greetings and honor be upon him. Then it is mentioned that the people after him wanted to build a tower reaching to heaven, and all of them agreed on this, because their language was one and their opinion was one. So God confused their tongues and scattered them from there over the face of the earth, and they did not build the city they had intended, and for this reason it was named Babel. Bubal, in Hebrew, means "dispersion."

As for what is in the tafsir of al-Baghawi and others, that 'Uj son of 'Unuq (vowelled as such, as in the Qamus) was in the time of Noah and was saved from the flood, and that the water did not rise above his knees, and similar claims, these are pure lies, contradicting His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾ [Hud: 37], and His saying: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy﴾ [Hud: 43], and His saying: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant﴾ [Nuh: 26], and the like. For everyone who mentioned that also mentioned that Moses (peace be upon him) killed him as a disbeliever.

The account of Noah (peace be upon him) from the Torah. He is Noah son of Lamech, son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Cainan, son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam (peace be upon him). This is in the early part of the first book of it: "Adam knew his wife, and she conceived and bore a son, and she named him Seth, and said: 'God has appointed me another offspring instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.' Cainan lived seventy years and begot Mahalalel. The total life of Cainan was nine hundred and ten years. Mahalalel lived sixty-five years and begot Jared. The total life of Mahalalel was eight hundred and ninety-five years. Jared lived one hundred and sixty-two years and begot Enoch. The total life of Jared was nine hundred and sixty-two years. Enoch lived sixty-five years and begot Methuselah. The total life of Enoch was three hundred and sixty-five years. Methuselah lived one hundred and eighty-seven years and begot Lamech. The total life of Methuselah was nine hundred and sixty-nine years. Lamech lived one hundred and eighty-two years and had a son, and he named him Noah, saying: "This one will give us rest from our work and from the toil of our hands on the ground which the Lord has cursed." The total days of the life of Lamech were seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died. Noah was five hundred years old, and Noah begot sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth. When men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them, the sons of the nobles saw the daughters of the common people, that they were very beautiful, and they took for themselves wives from among them, whomever they chose and loved. God then said: "My care and compassion shall no longer be for these people, because they follow the desires of the body and the flesh." There were giants on the earth in those days and afterwards, because the sons of the nobles went in to the daughters of the common people, and they bore them mighty men who were famous. The Lord saw that the evil of men had multiplied on the earth, and that the inclination of their thoughts and their malice was wicked all the days. The Lord said: "I will blot out the people whom I have created from the face of the new earth, both men and beasts, and even the creeping things and the birds of heaven." But Noah found favor with God and mercy and kindness. Noah was a righteous man, pious in his generation, and he pleased God. The earth was corrupt before God and filled with wickedness and debauchery. The Lord God saw that the earth had become corrupt, and God said to Noah: "The end of all people has come before Me, and the evil of their deeds, because the earth has been filled with wickedness and debauchery through their evil conduct. Behold, I am going to destroy them along with the earth. Make for yourself an ark of square timber, of gopher wood (in another copy: cypress), and make cells in the ark, and coat it with pitch inside and out. The length of the ship shall be three hundred cubits, its breadth fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits. Make a window in the ark, and its width at the top shall be one cubit. Place the door of the ark in its side, and make it with lower, middle and upper decks. Behold, I am going to bring a flood of waters upon the earth to destroy under heaven all flesh in which is the breath of life, and everything that is on the earth will perish. But I will establish My covenant with you. You shall enter the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you. And of every living thing of all flesh, two of every sort, you shall bring into the ark to keep them alive with you; they shall be male and female. Of the birds according to their kinds, and of the animals according to their kinds, and of every creeping thing of the ground according to its kind, two of every sort shall come to you to keep them alive. Take with you of every kind, two by two, to keep them alive, male and female. Also take with you of every food that is eaten, and store it up, and it shall be food for you and for them." Noah did everything just as God commanded him. Then God said to Noah: "Enter, you and all your household, into the ark, for I have found you righteous and pious in this generation. Of every clean animal take with you seven pairs, male and female, and of the animals that are not clean take with you two, male and female. Of the clean birds, seven pairs, male and female, and of the birds that are not clean, two by two, male and female, so that offspring may live on the face of the earth. For in seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will blot out every living thing that I have made from the face of the earth." Noah did as the Lord God commanded him. When seven days after that had passed, the waters of the flood came upon the earth. The fountains of the great deep burst forth and the windows of heaven were opened. The rain fell on the earth for forty days and forty nights. On that very day Noah and Shem, Ham and Japheth, the sons of Noah, and Noah's wife and the wives of his three sons, entered the ark with him, they and all the wild animals according to their kinds, and all the cattle according to their kinds, and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth according to its kind, and all the birds according to their kinds. There went into the ark with Noah, from every sparrow and from every winged creature, two by two, and from every creature of flesh in which is the spirit of life, two by two. Those that went in, of all flesh, went in male and female, as God had commanded Noah. Then the Lord God shut him in. The flood was on the earth forty days and forty nights. The waters increased and lifted up the ark, and it rose high above the earth. The waters grew very deep and increased greatly on the earth, [and the ark floated upon the face of the waters, and the waters prevailed very greatly upon the face of the earth, very greatly]. All the high and lofty mountains under heaven were covered. The waters rose fifteen cubits above the mountains. Every creature of flesh that was on the earth perished, birds, wild animals, cattle, every creeping thing that creeps on the earth, and all mankind. Everything on the dry land in whose nostrils was the breath of life died. Noah and those with him in the ark remained, and the waters prevailed on the earth for one hundred and fifty days. God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and cattle and all the birds that were with him in the ark. God caused a wind to blow over the earth, and the waters subsided and the rain stopped. The fountains of the deep and the windows of heaven were closed. The waters receded after one hundred and fifty days. The ark rested, and on the seventeenth day of the seventh month it settled on the mountains of Qudi. The waters continued to recede and decrease until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains appeared. After forty days, Noah opened the window he had made in the ark and sent out the raven, and it went out and kept going back and forth until the waters had dried up from the earth. [Then he sent out the dove after it to see whether the waters had lessened on the face of the earth.] But the dove found no place to set her foot, so she returned to the ark, for the waters were still on the face of the earth. He put out his hand, took her, and brought her into the ark, and waited seven more days. Then he sent out the dove again, and she came back to him toward evening, and in her beak was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters had subsided from the earth. He waited seven more days, and sent out the dove, and she did not return to him again. Then Noah removed the covering of the ark and looked, and behold, the surface of the ground was dry. God spoke to Noah and said to him: "Go out of the ark, you and your wife and your sons and your sons' wives with you, and all the wild animals that are with you, of all flesh, the birds and the cattle, and bring out every creeping thing that creeps on the earth with you, that they may breed abundantly on the earth and be fruitful and multiply on the earth." So Noah went out with those mentioned, and he built an altar to the Lord and took of all the clean cattle and birds and offered burnt offerings on the altar to the Lord God. The Lord God said: "I will never again curse the ground because of man, for the inclination of man's heart is evil from his youth. Nor will I again destroy every living thing as I have done. As long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, shall not cease." God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them: "Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth. Let the fear and dread of you fall upon all the wild animals of the earth, all the birds of the heavens, every creature that creeps on the ground, and all the fish of the sea; into your hand they are delivered. Every moving thing that lives shall be food for you; I give you all things, as I gave you the green plants. But you shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood. Surely for your lifeblood I will require a reckoning: from every beast I will require it, and from man, from every man's brother, I will require the life of man. Whoever sheds man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God He made man. And you, be fruitful and multiply, increase abundantly on the earth and multiply in it." God said to Noah and his sons with him: "Behold, I establish My covenant with you and with your descendants after you, and with every living creature that is with you, the birds, the cattle, and every wild animal of the earth with you, all that came out of the ark. I establish My covenant with you: never again shall all flesh be cut off by the waters of the flood, nor shall there again be a flood to destroy the earth." God said to Noah: "This is the sign of the covenant which I am making between Me and you and every living creature that is with you, for all future generations. I have set My bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth. When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow appears in the clouds, I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of all flesh, and never again shall the waters become a flood to destroy all flesh." The sons of Noah who went out of the ark with him were Shem, Ham and Japheth. [Ham was the father of Canaan.] These three were the sons of Noah, and from them the people were scattered over all the earth. Then it is mentioned that Noah (peace be upon him) slept, and Ham saw his nakedness and told his two brothers. Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it on their shoulders, walked backward, and covered their father's nakedness. When Noah learned what his youngest son had done, he cursed him, saying that he would be a servant to his brothers. The total days of Noah's life were nine hundred and fifty years. Then he died, peace, blessings, greetings and honor be upon him. Then it is mentioned that the people after him wanted to build a tower reaching to heaven, and all of them agreed on this, because their language was one and their opinion was one. So God confused their tongues and scattered them from there over the face of the earth, and they did not build the city they had intended, and for this reason it was named Babel. Bubal, in Hebrew, means "dispersion."

As for what is in the tafsir of al-Baghawi and others, that 'Uj son of 'Unuq (vowelled as such, as in the Qamus) was in the time of Noah and was saved from the flood, and that the water did not rise above his knees, and similar claims, these are pure lies, contradicting His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾ [Hud: 37], and His saying: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy﴾ [Hud: 43], and His saying: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant﴾ [Nuh: 26], and the like. For everyone who mentioned that also mentioned that Moses (peace be upon him) killed him as a disbeliever.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verse 49:

When this story had been completed in its full form, clarifying the striving of Nuh (peace be upon him) in conveying the warning without regard to whether people turned toward or away from him, and it was, along with that, indicative of complete knowledge and of an awareness of subtleties that has no path to it except through the All-Knowing King, it is then clearer than the sun in removing confusion about his (ﷺ) affair. Almighty Allah said, drawing attention to this: ﴿That﴾, i.e., these accounts, wondrous in their matter, strange in their affair, far beyond the reach of the opponent, and lofty in rank beyond the grasp of any who would take hold of them, ﴿are among the tidings of the unseen﴾, i.e., its great reports. Then He indicated that He continues to renew similar things for him, using the present tense in His saying: ﴿We reveal them to you﴾. It is as if it were said: some of the People of the Book know some of its details, so He indicated that all of it is unseen, and that what they know is a relative unseen, by His saying: ﴿You did not know them﴾, i.e., in this detail, ﴿you﴾. And since their being hidden from his people was evidence of their being hidden from him, because he had not mixed with others, He said: ﴿nor did your people﴾, i.e., even though they were people of strength in carrying out what they attempted and of great numbers, and among them are those who write and mix with scholars.

Since the time of that being hidden from them, although it was general for them, was some of the past time, He introduced the preposition and said: ﴿before this﴾, i.e., before My revelation to you, so that the suspicion would then arise that you had learned them from one of them, even though the People of the Book know much of them, as you have seen from the text of the Torah. Thus it became clear that your people have no aim except obstinacy. ﴿So be patient﴾ over that, and do not slacken in conveying the warning, for the final outcome will be yours just as it was for Nuh, because of his piety. ﴿Indeed, the final outcome﴾, i.e., the end of the matter, of success, victory and happiness, ﴿is for the God-fearing﴾, i.e., those who are steadfast in the fear of Allah at every time. The story has included the clarification of what the condition of the people of good and faith, and the people of evil and transgression, necessitates, as a lesson from the report about both groups, so that one may choose the condition of the former and guard against the condition of the latter, because of the evil outcome in this world and the Hereafter.

When that which is sufficient for the purpose of the surah had been completed, and it was concluded with the statement that the final outcome always belongs to the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), He followed it with evidence for this from the stories of the prophets, while fulfilling what the story of Noah, peace be upon all of them, was brought for, namely the urging to openly proclaim the warning. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And to﴾, meaning: And indeed We sent to ﴿ʿAd, their brother﴾, and He clarified it by saying: ﴿Hud﴾. Since the matter of Noah with his people had already preceded, the listener was eager to know whether what Hud, peace be upon him, said was like what Noah said or not. So He resumed the answer with His words: ﴿He said: O my people﴾, who are the most honored of people to me, ﴿worship Allah﴾, meaning: the One of majesty and generosity, alone. Then He made it explicit and gave the reason, saying: ﴿You have no﴾ ﴿god other than Him﴾, meaning: no deity worthy of worship besides Him. He went to the extreme in negation, saying: ﴿other than Him﴾. Thus he called them to the foundation of the religion, as is the practice of all the prophets and messengers. Then he concluded this by confronting them with what would displease them of the truth, and neither hope nor fear turned him away from that, so He said: ﴿You are only inventors of falsehood﴾, meaning: [you are] deliberately lying against Allah in associating others with Him, glory be to Him. This is because the evidences of reason supporting tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) are not hidden from any sensible person, so how much more so with the reminder of revelation! That refutes whoever associates partners with Allah, meaning: beware of the punishment of the one who fabricates.

Then he denied that he had any aim in this other than advising them, by his saying [in place of: "I am a sincere advisor to you in this matter, so let not my confronting you with what you dislike upset you"]: ﴿O my people﴾, repeating it to win their affection; ﴿I do not ask of you﴾, that is, in the future, just as I did not ask of you in the past; ﴿any wage for it﴾, that is, for this warning; so I am not open to suspicion; ﴿my wage is only﴾ [that is, nothing but]; ﴿from Him who created me﴾. [Then he described the One upon whom he relied, glorified be He, with what indicates sufficiency, so that thanking Him becomes obligatory upon me, and said]: ﴿Except upon He who originated me﴾, that is, who began my creation, and no one shared with Him in creating me. Hence He is the absolutely Self-Sufficient; I do not direct my desire to anyone else, as is obligatory for every person by virtue of it being the natural disposition (fitrah).

Since the dispute, in which there is no share of worldly benefit, does not require a person, in indicating that its one (the Lord) is a refuge to whom one turns from God's side, and that there is no salvation except through Him, to anything beyond reason, he based upon this saying of his the rebuke against them in his words: ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verse 52:

When he called them, pointing to their intimidation and taking the sincerity of his message as proven by his having no ulterior aim, he encouraged them to persist in fear of what had passed, by his saying: ﴿And O my people﴾, and they are (p-308) the most beloved of people to me, and they have the capacity for what is asked of them: ﴿Ask your Lord for forgiveness﴾, that is, seek His forgiveness by obeying Him, for what is due to Him because of His kindness to you. He indicated the high rank of repentance by the particle of delay, saying: ﴿Then turn to Him in repentance﴾, meaning: aspire to the lofty level of this rank by seeking God's concealment of your sins, then return to His obedience through regret, abandoning sin, and persistence. ﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundant showers﴾, that is, the water descending from it, or the clouds with water, ﴿in torrents﴾, that is, pouring down with abundant, continuous rain. ﴿And He will add strength to your strength﴾, that is, great strength combined ﴿to your strength﴾. Then he joined to his saying "Ask forgiveness" his saying: ﴿And do not turn away﴾, that is, do not burden yourselves with what you were not created for, of the soundness of submission, so that you exaggerate in turning away, as indicated by the affirmation of the ta' [in the verb form], ﴿as sinners﴾, that is, severing yourselves, by building your affairs upon corrupt assumptions about the good things of this world and the Hereafter.

When he had sincerely advised them with the utmost clarity, their response was only that **﴿they said﴾**, meaning that after he had shown them miracles of a kind that humankind has believed in, **﴿O Hud﴾** (they called him by his name, out of harshness and rudeness) **﴿you have not brought us any clear proof﴾**. In this they made plain to every person of understanding that they were obstinately rejecting sound reason and clear transmitted evidence. They were thus liars, just as the Arabs used to say to the Prophet ﷺ, after he had brought them signs through his hand in countless numbers, **"Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"** (p-٣٠٩) **﴿And we are not﴾**, and they went to extremes in negation and said: **﴿abandoning our gods﴾** (going beyond them or turning away from them) **﴿on your word﴾**. They left out the conjunction with the particle الفاء (fa'), which indicates that the first clause is the cause of the second, and used the conjunction الواو (waw) in their words **﴿and we are not for you﴾**, meaning specifically for you. They went to extremes in negation again and said **﴿believers﴾**. This shows that they abandoned following him out of stubborn opposition, not because they believed that he had brought no proof. [This is also indicated by their use of the nominal sentence (jumla ismiyya), which denotes permanence; so when it is negated, the underlying state is not negated.] A bayyina (clear proof) is a manifest argument that distinguishes truth from falsehood. Bayan (clarity) is the separation of a meaning from others until it appears to the mind freed from anything else. What drives people to abandon a clear proof after it has become apparent is either the blocking of doubt from reaching it, or following leaders in rejecting it, or accusing the one who brings it, or holding corrupt principles that lead to denying it, or obstinacy born of envy and the like. What unites all of these is the existence of doubt.

When they uttered this statement, whose corruption is evident, without attempting to refute what he had said with any kind of doubt, it was as if it were said to them: "What I have told you is no clearer or more just than it. Suppose its truth had not become apparent to you. What then do you say? That he was moved to it, even though it entails rejecting you, and you are my paternal cousins and the people most dear to me?" They said: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾. That is, it befell you and overtook you with an overtaking that clung to you as a handle clings to what it is attached to, with deliberate intent and force. ﴿Some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾, such as madness and derangement of mind. That, they said, is what drives you to forbid worshipping them.

(p-310) Since human nature requires that a person fear one who has harmed him, especially when he imagines that the other is able to harm him, one does not confront such a person with what he dislikes. [Their statement was stirring the listener to seek to learn his answer to them, so God, glorified is He, resumed reporting it with His words]: ﴿He said﴾, denying what they had said and making clear that their gods have no power to benefit them in any way. He emphasized it, because they were in a state where they did not think that anyone would say what he had said: ﴿Indeed, I call God to witness﴾, that is, the Supreme King, so that my excuse may be established before Him. [Out of courtesy toward God, he turned away from saying "and I call you to witness," lest it be supposed that He and they were equal, and shifted to the imperative form, showing contempt for them, and said]: ﴿and bear witness﴾, [that is] you yourselves, so that the proof may be established against you, for whichever of you it is. And so that your weakness may become evident, and everyone may know that you are in a state where you are treated with contempt, along with your religion, and no one cares about you or about it. ﴿Indeed, I am free from what you associate﴾ [Hud 11:54]. He made clear their baseness with His words: ﴿other than Him﴾ [Hud 11:55], whatever and whoever they are. How much more so when they are nothing but inanimate objects.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 11, verses 55–56:

﴿Then scheme against me﴾ all of you together, that is, separately if you wish, or gathered, you and your gods.

When immediate action in war is more terrifying, and its matter more difficult and dangerous, he showed its magnitude by using the particle of delay and said: ﴿Then give me no respite.﴾ Kayd (scheming) is seeking to vex by secret means in deceit. This verse is among the clear signs of prophethood for Hud, peace be upon him. It is as if it were said: suppose our gods are nothing; what drove you to be bold in opposing us, when we are many and strong, and you are no more than one of us? He said: ﴿Indeed I⦆ that is, I dared to do so because ﴿I have put my trust﴾ relying ﴿in Allah﴾, the King, whose punishment is feared, who has no king besides Him and no lord other than Him. He showed the comprehensiveness of His dominion by saying: ﴿My Lord and your Lord﴾, that is, the One who brought us into being and managed our affairs before He created us, so He knows what each of us does with regard to the Hereafter. For ﴿there is no creature﴾ that is, small or large, ﴿except that He holds its forelock﴾ that is, takes it with domination and overpowering, ﴿[i.e.,] has power over it.﴾ The seizing by the forelock has become customary as an expression of power, because all move according to His will and not according to their own will; indeed no one is free of disliking some of what he is in. This decisively shows that it is not by its own will but by a compelling will that overpowers it, and that is the Supreme King, glory be to Him. The forelock is the hair of the front of the head, and whoever is seized by the forelock has submitted to being taken and cannot incline. ﴿Indeed, my Lord⦆ that is, because my Lord, who has been good to me by setting me in what I am in, ﴿is on a path﴾ that is, a wide, clear way ﴿straight﴾, its matter evident to everyone, with no ambiguity at all, no flaw, no confusion, and no crookedness in any respect. Therefore every being in existence worships Him, calls upon Him, fears Him and hopes in Him, even if some of them take partners besides Him. As for what is worshipped besides Him, none magnifies it except its worshipper, and to one who is not its worshipper it has no weight at all. Thus it is established by this that He prevails over every thing with a dominance that every existent knows without any concealment at all; so He is the One hoped in and feared by the agreement of the wise, unlike your objects of worship. The sum is that the straight path requires manifestness, and so it requires the absence of disagreement, since ambiguity is absent. Whoever is upon it is of high standing, of renowned affair, perceptive of what he intends, with steadfastness and firmness, feared in his consequence, sought for following and love. Whoever does not turn toward it goes astray, and whoever turns away from it is seized, because of the multitude of His helpers and the might of His authority. Thus His power to protect whoever relies on Him is manifest, and the helplessness of their gods with them is manifest, because the forelocks of all are in His hand, and He is their Lord and the Lord of everything. The close of the verse thus corresponds to their words: ﴿You have brought us no clear proof﴾ [Hud: 53], as a rejection of it, because whoever is upon a straight path has no matter more evident than his; and it corresponds perfectly to his reply regarding his trust and what is within its scope. The forelock is the front part of the hair of the head, and its root is connection, from the saying: a desert (mafazah) adjoins (tanasi) another desert, when they are connected to one another.
